| |
## Kitchen Table Tuesday.
The Conforti Brief.
District-First Events.
---
| |
### Educate. Inform. Invite.
---
| |
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |
# Kitchen Table Tuesday
---
| | **Educating and connecting** with voters on important issues.
---
| | |
---
| | Our communities are facing an unprecedented crisis, as Illinois' 6th Congressional District has been ranked as having **some of the most fentanyl-related deaths in recent studies.** This alarming reality requires immediate and decisive action to address the devastating toll it is taking on our families. We must prioritize measures that will protect the district’s children from the "deadly grasp" of a drug that is currently killing our community members.
.To combat this epidemic, my goal in Congress is to **implement stronger penalties for fentanyl crimes and create task forces to target the source of illicit drugs.** By aggressively pursuing the criminal networks responsible for bringing these dangerous substances into our state, we can cut off the supply at its roots and hold the perpetrators accountable. We cannot afford to wait while this crisis escalates; it is time to secure our district and ensure a safer future for all Illinoisans.
---
| |
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | |
## The Conforti Brief
---
| | **Informing voters** on current events and how Niki plans to help them once in office.
---
| | The Radical Socialist Threat to the 6th District
.Recently, a former Clinton official sounded the alarm in the news, warning that a **"radical" socialist takeover will "destroy" the Democratic Party** if it is left unchecked. According to the article, far-left movements like the Democratic Socialists of America are attempting to use the party as a vehicle to launch their radical platform nationwide.
.This far-left shift is not just a national issue—it is actively harming families right here in Illinois' 6th Congressional District. Incumbent Democrat **Sean Casten recently voted against a measure that would have condemned socialism.** Instead of focusing on policies that benefit the hardworking people of the 6th District, Congressman Casten is more concerned with messaging and satisfying the more radical elements of his party.
. The economic consequences of this radical agenda are devastating. Casten pushes for increased spending on nonessential programs that benefit people in foreign countries, while forgetting about hardworking American families. Because of his failures in reining in wasteful spending, **Casten has earned the "Big Spender" designation** from the National Taxpayers Union. This unchecked borrowing adds to the national debt to pay for the Left's radical spending, placing an enormous and unsustainable burden on our children and grandchildren.
. Niki Conforti is running for Congress because **we need to curb this reckless spending and stop tax increases** on working families. When elected, she will take direct action to address this crisis by:
.
* 1\. **Implementing Spending Caps:** Niki will push for spending caps to limit the amount we add to the national debt in order to pay for the Left's radical spending.
* 2\. **Stopping Tax Hikes:** More spending inevitably leads to more taxes. Niki will work to curb the spending in Washington, D.C. and stop tax increases on working families.
* 3\. **Holding the Line on the Debt Ceiling:** Niki is opposed to raising the Debt Ceiling, and she will push to curb spending and limit the debt we incur as a Nation.
.

We cannot tax and spend our way to prosperity. It is time for sensible solutions that protect your wallet and secure our nation's financial future.

Stay informed on this issue—[**read the full breakdown here.**](https://us.list-manage.com/HMIJU0vsNiX?e=25f4fa3311&c2id=7b058fb5598c3e136d157ed790328086)

# District-First
# Events
---
| | **Inviting voters** to community events and how they can get involved!**
**Join the Conforti Campaign at**Coffee with Niki Conforti!**
---
| |
---
| | **Coffee with Niki Conforti
.**Looking for a casual setting to talk about the issues that matter most to your family? Grab a cup of coffee and join Niki for a one-on-one conversation about reining in reckless government spending, cutting red tape for small businesses, and protecting local communities.

* **Date:** Thursday, August 6, 2026
* **Time:** 6:00 PM – 8:00 PM
* **Location:** Krema Coffee in Tinley Park, IL
*
.

**Community Discussion on Energy - Crisis or Opportunity
.**Come out to show your support for our "district-first" mentality and join the community for this important occasion. High energy costs are identified as a primary driver of the current high cost-of-living in our district. As an energy consultant, Niki understands exactly why this is happening and how to fix it.
.
* **Date:** Tuesday, August 11, 2026
* **Time:** 7:00 PM
* **Location:** Elmhurst American Legion THB 187 (310 W Butterfield Road, Elmhurst, IL)

Get Involved: Bring your family, friends, and neighbors to these events to learn more about our District-First vision. For more information, please contact our team at [**info@conforti4congress.com.**](mailto:info@conforti4congress.com?subject=Event%3A%20Coffee%20with%20Niki%20%2F%20Community%20Discussion%20on%20Energy&body=)

We look forward to seeing you there!

| | Friend,
July 31st is coming up fast — it's our last fundraising deadline before District 24 heads to the polls on August 18th.
Here's a quick look at what I've been up to in Tallahassee:
* Serving on **Ways & Means** to keep an eye on your tax dollars
* Sitting on the **Select Committee on Property Taxes** , because owning your home should mean actually owning it
* Helping **bring millions of dollars** back into our local nonprofits — the food banks, shelters, and community groups that keep this district running

None of that happens without support from people like you. This week, that support goes further than usual.
Every dollar between now and July 31st helps send a clear message: District 24 is paying attention.
$25. $50. $250. Whatever you can give makes a difference this week.

[**DONATE HERE**](https://us.list-manage.com/8swcIhwhUIT?e=d1c1b9864f&c2id=d3808649044f505f0f4143aac3cd50ac&m=9MspKn7zKyV839xg6h51TgJ3bE8t__CMlQ5Qn09HizRDozTGVeWwCCkgUTc=)
Thank you for standing with me. Let's finish this the right way.

clean_body: Your support would go a long way to help Democracy Defenders compete in these races | Peter, This is a wake-up call — ad spending in Ohio alone is expected to reach a record $749 million for the midterm elections! | = We need to talk about why interest groups are so focused on one state. On top of a hotly contested Senate race, Ohio will see a handful of consequential elections for the future of democracy — including the fourth-most expensive gubernatorial election in the country. The elections for governor, auditor, and secretary of state will determine how the redistricting crisis plays out because they all hold crucial positions on the state’s redistricting commission. These are the officials who will determine if fair maps are drawn in the future. The fair maps movement has endorsed a slate of Democracy Defenders in Ohio and other key states across the country. This wasn't an oversight.

| Fight for Reform is dedicated to electing Democrats, transforming our broken campaign finance system, and ending _Citizens United_ state by state. If you would like to get fewer emails, [**_click here._**](https://act.fightforreform.org/go/59469?t=1&akid=24608%2E4449941%2EGBrAyj) If you would like to unsubscribe, [**_click here._**](https://act.fightforreform.org/go/59470?t=2&akid=24608%2E4449941%2EGBrAyj) [](https://act.fightforreform.org/go/75232?t=3&akid=24608%2E4449941%2EGBrAyj) Team,

Growing up in Allagash and spending years working 80-hour weeks in the woods to make ends meet, I know firsthand what working Mainers need from our government.

And for 30 years, Susan Collins has failed us. Time and again, she has sold us out to Donald Trump and his MAGA agenda while pretending we’re too dumb to notice. [**And I’m sick of it.**](https://act.fightforreform.org/go/75232?t=4&akid=24608%2E4449941%2EGBrAyj)

My name is Troy Jackson. I’m a proud Mainer, father, and fifth-generation logger.

[**This weekend, I officially earned the Democratic nomination for U.S. Senate. Now it’s time to defeat Susan Collins and her billionaire backers. So I’m asking you to split a donation between my campaign and Fight For Reform to become a Founding Donor to my campaign right now and help us win the most important Senate race in the country.**](https://act.fightforreform.org/go/75232?t=5&akid=24608%2E4449941%2EGBrAyj) | [DONATE NOW >>](https://act.fightforreform.org/go/75232?t=6&akid=24608%2E4449941%2EGBrAyj)
---
Team, let me tell you a bit about what this race means to me.

When I was growing up, I was a poor kid in a town full of poor kids. My family relied on food assistance at times. I distinctly remember when I was 13 years old, we didn’t have heat or running water, and I heard my mother quietly crying to herself, wishing she could do more for us.

After high school, I became a logger like my dad, and his dad, and his dad before him. When a greedy landowner tried to screw my fellow loggers and me out of fair wages, I fought back. A whole bunch of politicians, including then-first-term Senator Susan Collins, promised to listen, but they left us high and dry — and I realized that nothing would change unless there were working-class voices in power.

So I ran for the Maine legislature, where I served 20 years, including six years as the President of the Maine Senate. It’s been the honor of my life to fight for working people.

I drove hours each way between the North Woods and the State Capitol, because that's what the job required. I won those elections in a district that went for Trump by 20 points, because up here, people care less about a label and more about whether you give a damn about their family.

Team, I’m building this campaign the right way. With grassroots support from folks like you. I’m not running to impress the billionaires or the corporate class. I’m running for the mom who’s worried about how she’ll fill her gas tank this week. I’m running for the kid whose whole life will be determined by the quality of his education. I’m running to ensure every working family in Maine has the government they deserve.

[**If you believe in this fight and our movement, I’m humbly asking you to split a donation between my campaign and Fight For Reform today to help us reach our fundraising goal and take on the GOP’s millions. Even $5 makes a difference >>**](https://act.fightforreform.org/go/75232?t=7&akid=24608%2E4449941%2EGBrAyj)

One year ago, I launched my campaign for the U.S. Senate.
It was not in my plans to go to Washington. In fact, when I left the Governor's office in January of last year, the first thing I did was rip off the tie and dress shoes and put on my MJ sneakers. I spent time at my farm, caught up on some reading and movies, watched sports and enjoyed being with my family.
The decision to run for US Senate wasn't easy, and I shared [why I decided to run](https://substack.com/redirect/84d9dc0b-04a3-40ac-8442-12d497d103db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with you all a couple weeks ago.
Today, I wanted to reflect upon my time on the trail since we launched this campaign last July.
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/209e6e64-9722-42f6-99c2-25223d343fb7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Volunteer](https://substack.com/redirect/50744f3e-f04d-4e98-8118-70f19fc3df56?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8fe1d511-6af4-439f-ac48-d4d20465a451?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

* * *
I've spent the last year talking with folks all across the state, visiting communities large and small and hearing from hardworking North Carolinians about what actually matters to them.
From Brasstown to Leland, North Carolinians have proven time and again their passion and resilience.
And since our launch, we've knocked more than 154,000 doors across the state and recruited more than 14,800 volunteers.
We have grown a grassroots movement focused on the needs of all North Carolinians. But the race is only going to get tougher as we head towards Election Day.
I am so fortunate to have an amazing group of people standing beside me, fighting for the future of North Carolina. Every time someone spends part of their Saturday knocking on doors, making calls, sending postcards or pitches in a few dollars, they are doing it because they believe that a better, stronger North Carolina and country are possible.
That promise keeps us going. I still believe our best days are ahead of us. And I believe you do too.
I can't wait to see you on the road.

| | No matter how broken the past may seem, God's redemption is always greater. This week on the Moms for America Podcast, we're sharing two powerful conversations recorded at CPAC with Victor and Eileen Marx, founders of All Things Possible Ministries. Victor shares how the Lord redeemed a childhood marked by horrific abuse, leading him to dedicate his life to rescuing vulnerable women and children around the world. He also discusses his campaign for Governor of Colorado and his vision for restoring trust in government, defending Colorado values, and helping families thrive. Alongside him, Eileen shares her own perspective as a devoted mom, humanitarian, author, and ministry leader. Together, their unwavering faith and commitment to serving others offer a powerful reminder that no life is beyond the reach of God's redeeming love. Don't miss this inspiring conversation that will strengthen your faith and renew your hope. name: Abdul El-Sayed
subject: A reporter tried to catch me
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Abdul for U
body:
[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1219?t=1001&akid=2753%2E251025%2EShG3Gk ]Abdul for US Senate [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1219?t=1002&akid=2753%2E251025%2EShG3Gk ]Abdul for US Senate

Peter, a reporter
asked me a question at our press conference that was designed to be a
little bit of a gotcha. It was actually a good question, too.

I've been loud about the dark money flooding into this race — the kind of
group that doesn't have to disclose donors. Over $59 million has been
spent to prop up our opponent, Haley Stevens. So, the reporter asked: have
I ever turned down support from a dark money group that wanted to back
*my* campaign?

Here's the honest answer I gave, and I want you to sit with it for a
second:

“I don't take those meetings, and they don't come to me in
the first place.”

That's not me dodging. That's the whole point.

Dark money doesn't knock on your door unless it knows you'll open it.
These groups don't waste a dollar. They spend because they know exactly
what they're trying to buy: a vote in the U.S. Senate.

* Big Pharma wants a senator who looks the other way on prescription
drug prices.
* Big Tech wants free rein to put data centers in our backyards and
raise our utility bills.
* AIPAC wants a vote to send $3.3 billion of your tax dollars overseas
instead of investing it in our schools and infrastructure.

They looked at our campaign, and they knew: there's nothing here for sale.
So they took their money elsewhere.

In fact, they've trucked $59 million into this primary against us, more
outside spending than any Democratic Senate primary candidate has ever
withstood in history. More than half of it comes from AIPAC.

Think about the opportunity cost of that money. You can eliminate medical
debt for a penny on the dollar. When I served in Wayne County, we started
the work of eliminating up to $700 million in medical debt. That $59
million could’ve wiped out roughly $5.9 billion in medical debt for
American families.

Instead, it's buying 30-second misleading ads.

So here's where you come in, and I need you to hear the urgency in this.
Our primary is on August 4th — exactly one week from today. That's all the
time we have left to prove that the many can beat the money.

This is the last stretch,
Peter. There won’t be another
primary day to make this case. Every dollar between now and August 4th
either answers their $59 million or it doesn't.

They have the money. We have the many. Our campaign runs on people like
you, because I’ve never taken corporate money and I never will.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260728-1-ak.7EBcAx&amount=10&refcode=em20260728-2752&t=1004&akid=2753%2E251025%2EShG3Gk ]Chip in $10 or any amount right now, before August 4th,
to prove that Michigan's Senate seat is not for sale.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260728-1-ak.7EBcAx&amount=10&refcode=em20260728-2752&t=1023&akid=2753%2E251025%2EShG3Gk ]Donate $10 ››

I know I ask a lot of you in these emails. But we're at the end of this
campaign now, and there is so little time left. So if you can help right
now, this is the moment. Thanks for reading this far, and for being part
of this.

Your friend in the fight,

Abdul

clean_body: [ ]Abdul for US Senate [ ]Abdul for US Senate Peter, a reporter asked me a question at our press conference that was designed to be a little bit of a gotcha. It was actually a good question, too. I've been loud about the dark money flooding into this race — the kind of group that doesn't have to disclose donors. Over $59 million has been spent to prop up our opponent, Haley Stevens. So, the reporter asked: have I ever turned down support from a dark money group that wanted to back my campaign? Here's the honest answer I gave, and I want you to sit with it for a second: “I don't take those meetings, and they don't come to me in the first place.” That's not me dodging. That's the whole point. Dark money doesn't knock on your door unless it knows you'll open it. These groups don't waste a dollar. They spend because they know exactly what they're trying to buy: a vote in the U.S. Senate. Big Pharma wants a senator who looks the other way on prescription drug prices. Big Tech wants free rein to put data centers in our backyards and raise our utility bills. * AIPAC wants a vote to send $3.3 billion of your tax dollars overseas instead of investing it in our schools and infrastructure. They looked at our campaign, and they knew: there's nothing here for sale. So they took their money elsewhere. In fact, they've trucked $59 million into this primary against us, more outside spending than any Democratic Senate primary candidate has ever withstood in history. More than half of it comes from AIPAC. Think about the opportunity cost of that money. You can eliminate medical debt for a penny on the dollar. When I served in Wayne County, we started the work of eliminating up to $700 million in medical debt. That $59 million could’ve wiped out roughly $5.9 billion in medical debt for American families. Instead, it's buying 30-second misleading ads. So here's where you come in, and I need you to hear the urgency in this. Our primary is on August 4th — exactly one week from today. That's all the time we have left to prove that the many can beat the money. This is the last stretch, Peter. There won’t be another primary day to make this case. Every dollar between now and August 4th either answers their $59 million or it doesn't. They have the money. We have the many. Our campaign runs on people like you, because I’ve never taken corporate money and I never will. [ ]Chip in $10 or any amount right now, before August 4th, to prove that Michigan's Senate seat is not for sale. [ ]Donate $10 ›› I know I ask a lot of you in these emails. But we're at the end of this campaign now, and there is so little time left. So if you can help right now, this is the moment. Thanks for reading this far, and for being part of this. Your friend in the fight, Abdul

# **Austria deports more migrants than tt receives asylum applications for first time in 20 years**
Austria recorded **[more deportations and removals than new asylum applications](https://substack.com/redirect/e94ffcb8-69bd-4fb5-8a55-9efb083f9df8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in the first half of 2026 -- the first time that's happened in over two decades.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e94ffcb8-69bd-4fb5-8a55-9efb083f9df8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Asylum applications dropped 44% compared to the same period last year,** with roughly 4,900 submitted between January and June, while over 7,000 migrants were removed during the same period. Interior Minister Gerhard Karner credited enhanced border controls and suspension of the family reunification program as the primary drivers.

* **The policy shift followed the Freedom Party of Austria 's historic 2024 election victory,** which pressured the coalition government to dramatically tighten immigration enforcement. Syrian approval rates collapsed from 67% two years ago to roughly one-third this year, and 27% of all asylum requests were outright rejected in the first half of 2026.
* **Austria is also pursuing third-country return hub agreements similar to Italy 's model.** FPÖ leader Herbert Kickl called for even stricter measures following Saturday's alleged Islamist van attack at Berlin's pride parade.

@NorahODonnell: The January 6th committee shows a draft executive order from Dec. 2020 that would direct the Secretary of Defense to seize voting machines immediately. [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/EA/EA007/1/89215/images/NOD_SeizeVotingMachines.png]
The January 6th committee showed evidence in a hearing that President Trump was going to order the Department of Defense to seize voting machines around the country to search for evidence of wrongdoing.
While the order was never given, this highlights the lengths some people were willing to go in their use of federal power to justify their fantasies about elections they see as "stolen". This comes despite the states having control of our elections, not the federal government.

# **▶️: Why I Support Medicare for All**
Healthcare shouldn't be a privilege reserved for those who can afford it.Recently, someone commented on one of my videos asking, "_Guess you forgot about the Affordable Care Act_?"[**_Watch the video below to hear why I believe the Affordable Care Act was an important first step—but not the final destination._**](https://1xz3r.mjt.lu/lnk/AVkAAKC9IG0AAc7VBDAAA-Neh6MAAYKKXNoAoUWGADIMFwBqaMWOfhViGJ5pQA2Rmt8uSLQ_lQAtq28/2/b6Gf0WDKAztkjS2cIdalCQ/aHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYWN0Ymx1ZS5jb20vZG9uYXRlL2xldHMtZmluaXNoLXRoaW5ncw)

The ACA expanded access to healthcare for millions of Americans, but too many families are still struggling with high premiums, deductibles, and prescription drug costs. No one should have to choose between seeing a doctor and paying their bills.That's why I support Medicare for All. I believe every American deserves access to affordable, quality healthcare, regardless of their income, employer, or zip code.**Healthcare is a basic human right—not a luxury.** If you believe it's time to finish the job and make healthcare truly affordable for every American, I hope you'll stand with me.Together, we can build a healthcare system that puts patients before profits.[**_If you're able, please consider making a contribution today. clean_body: The ACA expanded access to healthcare for millions of Americans, but too many families are still struggling with high premiums, deductibles, and prescription drug costs. | | ▶️: Why I Support Medicare for All Healthcare shouldn't be a privilege reserved for those who can afford it.Recently, someone commented on one of my videos asking, "Guess you forgot about the Affordable Care Act?" | The ACA expanded access to healthcare for millions of Americans, but too many families are still struggling with high premiums, deductibles, and prescription drug costs. No one should have to choose between seeing a doctor and paying their bills.That's why I support Medicare for All. I believe every American deserves access to affordable, quality healthcare, regardless of their income, employer, or zip code.Healthcare is a basic human right—not a luxury. If you believe it's time to finish the job and make healthcare truly affordable for every American, I hope you'll stand with me.Together, we can build a healthcare system that puts patients before profits. | *If you"ve saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | | | | Thank you for your continuous support.\- Laura | | | | | | Paid for by Laura Jones for Congress P.O. body:
The numbers are in, and Hughes/Gettys leads where it counts most.

| | | | |
---
| | Alaskan Dollars, Alaskan Values, Alaskan Ticket
---
**Greetings, Fellow Alaskans and Friends: **
**A new analysis of campaign finance data tells a story that no ad buy can manufacture: Hughes/Gettys ranks first among gubernatorial candidates for in-state donors and in-state dollars. That's not a talking point; it's the State of Alaska Public Offices Commission (APOC) report. This ticket is funded by Alaskans, run by Alaskans donating their professional expertise, focused entirely on Alaskans, and that's exactly how it should be.**** ****With three weeks until August 18th, the case is straightforward. No outside consultants collecting six-figure salaries. No high negatives. No baggage. What we have is a demonstrated record, a concrete action plan, and the kind of grassroots coalition that wins general elections. On the issues, we're not vague: from reforming game management to treat wildlife as food security rather than a luxury, to asking the hard questions about why young Alaskans are leaving and what it will take to keep them here, this campaign is built on real policy and real conversations.**** ****The people who are showing up, writing handwritten notes, decking out stuffed moose in campaign merch, and endorsing this ticket from Mat-Su to Anchorage to Fairbanks and across the state know what's at stake. Scroll down for parade highlights, featured supporters, and everything that made this week another strong step forward.**
---
**p.s. We're just now 3 short weeks away from the Primary Election on August 18, and we truly need every Alaskan for the Hughes/Gettys ticket to rally behind us big time! Donations are needed to win the upcoming primary set us up for victory in November as well. If you can, please give and any amount can have an impact in this election. We know not all supporters can a monetary gift, but we can use your help as a volunteer, with sign placement on your property and/or business, going door-to-door to your Alaskan neighbors to get out and vote for the best team for the job, help with donation calls, or write an endorsement. This is a call for critical support action today - reach out to us at **[**info@alaskansforhughes.com**](mailto:info@alaskansforhughes.com)** and let us know how you would like to join us or simply donate using the button below!**
**Ready to serve you,**

**In-state patronage indicates votes. Out-of-state patronage does NOT indicate votes. More Alaskans every day are recognizing that the Hughes/Gettys ticket is the top contender that can beat the Democrat ticket in November hands-down. No skeletons, no baggage, no high negatives that are plaguing other candidates. Shelley Hughes and Blake Gettys: demonstrated leadership, an action plan, integrity, a track record of getting things done. Ready to take Alaska to the next level!**
**Hitting the news cycle on Monday, July 27, analysis of donations from the latest APOC report shows Hughes is the top candidate for in-state donors. From Natalie Spaudling at Must Read Alaska:**
**"It is hardly a secret that money plays a role in shaping a public official’s loyalties, which makes Alaskans wary of candidates who rely on out-of-state funding. How are the gubernatorial candidates stacking up in terms of Alaskan vs. out-of-state patronage?**

Our team consists of Alaskans who’ve been at the management level of numerous statewide campaigns and they are donating their professional expertise to the Hughes/Gettys ticket. **
**Dollars donated go to getting our message out and engaging with voters. We could certainly use a few more of those dollars to get through the next three weeks to ensure we make it into the Top 4. **Bottom line, if you don’t want a Democrat to win, please support Hughes/Gettys!"**** -** **Shelley Hughes**

**Alaska’s current game management framework has drifted from the constitutional requirement to manage wildlife for maximum sustained yield for humans. The existing mission of the Department of Fish & Game (DF&G) does not prioritize food security, abundance, or predator–prey balance needed to support robust ungulate populations. A re‐aligned, abundance‐focused policy direction is necessary to ensure that Alaskans’ kitchen‐table resources remain reliable and plentiful.**** ****Policy & Plans:**

* **Rededicate the mission of the Department of Game (DG)**
* **Appoint a Game Manager as Commissioner of Fish and Game focused on abundance**
* **Modernize game management with advanced technology**
* **Reform the Board of Game (BOG) for timeliness, transparency, and reliability**
* **Prioritize predator control & intensive management**
* **Expand habitat & access projects**
* **Strengthen local Advisory Committees (ACs)**
* **Expand partnerships for science, funding, and workforce development**
* **Clarify subsistence & state authority **

clean_body: The numbers are in, and Hughes/Gettys leads where it counts most. | | | | | | | Alaskan Dollars, Alaskan Values, Alaskan Ticket Greetings, Fellow Alaskans and Friends: A new analysis of campaign finance data tells a story that no ad buy can manufacture: Hughes/Gettys ranks first among gubernatorial candidates for in-state donors and in-state dollars. That's not a talking point; it's the State of Alaska Public Offices Commission (APOC) report. This ticket is funded by Alaskans, run by Alaskans donating their professional expertise, focused entirely on Alaskans, and that's exactly how it should be. With three weeks until August 18th, the case is straightforward. No outside consultants collecting six-figure salaries. No high negatives. No baggage. What we have is a demonstrated record, a concrete action plan, and the kind of grassroots coalition that wins general elections. On the issues, we're not vague: from reforming game management to treat wildlife as food security rather than a luxury, to asking the hard questions about why young Alaskans are leaving and what it will take to keep them here, this campaign is built on real policy and real conversations. The people who are showing up, writing handwritten notes, decking out stuffed moose in campaign merch, and endorsing this ticket from Mat-Su to Anchorage to Fairbanks and across the state know what's at stake. Scroll down for parade highlights, featured supporters, and everything that made this week another strong step forward. p.s. We're just now 3 short weeks away from the Primary Election on August 18, and we truly need every Alaskan for the Hughes/Gettys ticket to rally behind us big time! Growing up in Allagash and spending years working 80-hour weeks in the woods to make ends meet, I know firsthand what working Mainers need from our government.
And for 30 years, Susan Collins has failed us. Time and again, she has sold us out to Donald Trump and his MAGA agenda while pretending we’re too dumb to notice. And I’m sick of it.
My name is Troy Jackson. I’m a proud Mainer, father, and fifth-generation logger.
This weekend, I officially earned the Democratic nomination for U.S. Senate. Now it’s time to defeat Susan Collins and her billionaire backers. So I’m asking you to split a donation between my campaign and Resist Reclaim Rebuild to become a Founding Donor to my campaign right now and help us win the most important Senate race in the country. Let me tell you a bit about what this race means to me.
When I was growing up, I was a poor kid in a town full of poor kids. My family relied on food assistance at times. I distinctly remember when I was 13 years old, we didn’t have heat or running water, and I heard my mother quietly crying to herself, wishing she could do more for us.
After high school, I became a logger like my dad, and his dad, and his dad before him. When a greedy landowner tried to screw my fellow loggers and me out of fair wages, I fought back. A whole bunch of politicians, including then-first-term Senator Susan Collins, promised to listen, but they left us high and dry — and I realized that nothing would change unless there were working-class voices in power.
So I ran for the Maine legislature, where I served 20 years, including six years as the President of the Maine Senate. It’s been the honor of my life to fight for working people.
I drove hours each way between the North Woods and the State Capitol, because that's what the job required. I won those elections in a district that went for Trump by 20 points, because up here, people care less about a label and more about whether you give a damn about their family.

# Iran
* **Attacks reported in Iraqi Kurdistan:** Iranian forces reportedly [launched](https://substack.com/redirect/6e42a58b-ad5c-4ef2-9ce3-60a6ce9aa702?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a wave of drones toward Iraq's Kurdistan Region on Monday night, with repeated explosions and interceptions reported over Erbil.
* Kurdish journalist Scharo Bajalan reported at least two impacts: one in the Alana Valley near Soran, where a Komala opposition camp is located, and another north of Erbil. He said drones were launched from both Iran and areas controlled by Iraq's Popular Mobilization Forces.
* Footage circulating online appeared to show U.S. forces intercepting at least one drone over Erbil. The extent of any casualties or damage remains unclear.
* **Explosions reported in Saudi Arabia; drone attacks on Jordan:** Explosions were [heard](https://substack.com/redirect/cc2c8369-70c9-40f6-ac85-21587fe8a1af?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in eastern Saudi Arabia and drones attacked Jordan overnight, an Iranian state-linked outlet reported on Tuesday.
* At least 6 "powerful explosions" struck the eastern region of Saudi Arabia near oil and gas facilities, Nour News, an outlet affiliated with Iran's Supreme National Security Council, reported early Tuesday. The Saudi government has not confirmed the attack
* In a separate report, the outlet said local sources had described "extensive" drone attacks in the eastern desert of Jordan.
* Jordan's military said it shot down a drone that entered its airspace over the eastern desert near the borders with Iraq and Saudi Arabia early Tuesday, without identifying its origin.
* Separately, the Israeli military said it intercepted a drone near the Jordanian border that did not enter Israeli airspace and that it was investigating where it was launched from.
* **Hormuz talks continue as Oman reportedly puts forward joint management proposal:** Iran, Oman, and Gulf states stepped up diplomatic efforts over the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday.
* Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi [held](https://substack.com/redirect/0fdc11cd-f2bb-446f-af79-773aac31a7e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) separate phone calls with Oman's Badr Albusaidi and Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud. According to IRNA, the ministers reviewed regional developments and stressed strengthening diplomatic cooperation to restore stability and address "insecurity" in the Strait.
* Oman [presented](https://substack.com/redirect/c2b59e7f-f25c-4c53-ad6b-585c67e52a6e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Iran with a proposal for a joint regional mechanism to manage the Strait of Hormuz with voluntary user fees, Reuters reported. Under the proposal, which reportedly has regional backing, Iran would no longer exercise sole control over the waterway.
* Foreign ministers from Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries also [held](https://substack.com/redirect/7d6a959e-1260-492b-9426-3b501e5933fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a virtual meeting on the ongoing U.S.-Iran negotiations on Tuesday. Oman's Foreign Ministry said they stressed the need for closer coordination on freedom and safety of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz while prioritising political and diplomatic solutions to strengthen regional security and stability.
* **Iranian FM spokesperson discusses U.S. "quagmire":** Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei [spoke](https://substack.com/redirect/85b3ffd2-ea37-4fa3-b8bf-c97511e51be2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to reporters on Monday about the U.S.' current position, saying that he did not believe they were "managing" the conflict well. "This war was supposed to force Iran to surrender," he said "but five months later they remain trapped in a quagmire."
* Baghaei reaffirmed that Iran would "not allow the United States to decide when war and peace begin and end."
* The spokesperson also [criticized](https://substack.com/redirect/ea5a47d9-5941-4265-80c1-47c93c4c699c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who announced actions this weekend against Russian ships he claimed were being used to transport supplies to Iran. Baghaei compared Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky's conduct to anarchists who carried out dramatic and dangerous acts before World War I, calling his actions "theatrical" and saying that they "exaggerated" his "limited weight in international affairs." "Zelenskyy's patrons must rein him in," he said.
* **Trump says that talks with Iran are "ongoing": **President Donald Trump [told](https://substack.com/redirect/f46468b5-0967-48a1-b110-07d8c0f2b824?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) reporters on Air Force One on Monday that the U.S. was in "very deep talks" with Iran, and that there was a "good chance" of reaching an agreement, but that military action could resume if no deal is reached, saying that the U.S. would "go back to what we were doing two days ago."
* Neither Tehran nor Washington acknowledged any direct meetings, but indirect talks primarily involving Iran and Oman, and secondarily involving Qatar, Pakistan, Egypt, and U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, reportedly remain ongoing, according to Axios. The current negotiations are focused on reopening the Strait of Hormuz and restarting talks on a comprehensive nuclear agreement, according to the outlet.
* Trump also [said](https://substack.com/redirect/e46e2864-155f-473c-8b3f-0c2ef57df22e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that the U.S. had "taken in billions and billions of dollars from Venezuela," and threatened that he would do the same with Iran. The comments follow reporting from the Financial Times last week that of the $13 billion in oil revenue seized by the U.S., $7 billion remains unaccounted for. When asked about this by reporters on Monday, he said the money he was being used to "run the country."
* **Shipping remains severely constrained in Hormuz and Babl-Mandab:** Windward [recorded](https://substack.com/redirect/dcc53488-1bc6-415f-88de-62097e22c9fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) seven Strait of Hormuz crossings on July 27, two of these inbound and five of them outbound, all using the northern Iran-run corridor.
* 14 vessels entered the Red Sea through the Bab Al-Mandab and 21 exited on July 26, Windward reported. Inbound traffic into the strait has collapsed by nearly 70%, and outbound traffic has fallen about 28%.
* **Two more executed in Iran:** Iran executed two men convicted on charges of killing police officers and damaging public properties during the mass protests in January, according to the state affiliated agency Mizan. The two men were identified as Abolfazl Sepahi Badjani and Amir Hossein Safari Hosseinabadi. Iran hanged two other men convicted in the same case earlier in July. Iran has executed dozens of people so far in 2026.

# Yemen
* **Ansarallah claims strike on major Saudi oil facility in Abqaiq:** Ansarallah [claimed](https://substack.com/redirect/5fda22cb-7e41-4e6d-8b97-06eda1d477c9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) responsibility on Monday for a drone strike on Saudi Aramco's Abqaiq crude-processing facility, the kingdom's largest.
* Abqaiq stabilizes the bulk of Saudi crude before export, making it one of the most critical nodes in the kingdom's oil infrastructure. It was also the target of the September 2019 drone and missile attack that briefly cut roughly 5% of global oil supply, causing a major shock in oil prices.
* Saudi Arabia's foreign ministry confirmed the attack, but attributed it to Iran-backed militias operating in Iraq.
* Ali Faleh al-Zaidi, Iraq's prime minister, [directed](https://substack.com/redirect/abb5423c-5ef0-42fb-8ae5-5afd5eba20cc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) security agencies to investigate Saudi Arabia's claim, according to the Iraqi News Agency. The Iraqi government said it would be examining the evidence and would pursue legal action against anyone found to have been involved
* **Saudi Aramco shuts down Jazan refinery after Ansarallah attack:** Saudi Aramco shut down its 400,000-barrel-per-day Jazan refinery following an Ansarallah attack, Reuters reported, citing consultancy IR. The attack reportedly damaged the refinery's integrated gasification combined-cycle (IGCC) complex and oil tank area, with repairs expected to allow an initial restart by August 15.

# Palestine
* **Killed and wounded in Gaza:** Over the past 24 hours, four Palestinians were killed--three in new attacks and one due to wounds sustained in earlier attacks--and 14 were injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health.
* The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,333 killed, with 174,023 injured. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,207 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 3,914, while 803 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble.
* **Israel attacks Gaza on Monday and Tuesday:**
* Israeli forces [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/da4791a4-75b8-4bc7-8ad2-bdced4e0a695?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) three Palestinians and wounded several others on Monday, shelling the northern and central parts of the Strip, according to Felesteen Online.
* An Israeli drone attack on Monday also wounded three fishermen near the Gaza port gate.
* An Israeli military vehicle [fired](https://substack.com/redirect/479384a8-727b-4b5f-a928-5407e0a5be9e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Deir-al-Balah on Tuesday, wounding two Palestinians, according to WAFA.
* **At least eight Palestinians killed since Thursday as Israeli raids and settler attacks escalate across the occupied West Bank:** Israeli forces and armed settlers continue to intensify their attacks across the occupied West Bank following Friday's settler attack in Tal. At least eight Palestinians, including a child, have been [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/9480394a-28a4-4b92-9489-e6f1ca4a4252?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) since Thursday, the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs reported. On Tuesday, raids, assaults, land seizures, and settler violence were reported across multiple governorates, according to WAFA, with at least 22 Palestinians detained by Israeli forces, according to the Palestinian Prisoners' Affairs office.
* **Bethlehem:** A Palestinian was [injured](https://substack.com/redirect/341158ff-c212-4007-b1b8-a337900b602f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) after Israeli settlers beat him with an iron pipe near Al-Minya village. Israeli forces separately raided Tuqu' and Husan.
* **Ramallah:** Israeli forces [raided](https://substack.com/redirect/5073c460-7af0-4def-a3a5-1c1060111645?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Shuqba, west of Ramallah, on Tuesday morning and demolished a residential building, leaving the families who lived there homeless.
* **Hebron:** Israeli settlers [assaulted](https://substack.com/redirect/8a5fa0df-a99b-4758-89cf-c894108e8be5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Palestinians in the Khallet Al-Hamam area of Yatta, beating residents and firing tear gas. Israeli forces arrested a Palestinian father and his two sons after the attack. Forces also demolished two residential buildings.
* A Palestinian man in Masafer Yatta [seized](https://substack.com/redirect/99a35c37-2919-4391-83e3-1c3cdf452034?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a weapon from a violent Israeli settler on Tuesday, becoming the third to attempt to do so in the last four days.
* **Salfit:** Israeli settlers [established](https://substack.com/redirect/d7b2859b-f677-48f2-b9e2-17ebcab62d1d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a new settlement outpost on Palestinian land in Yasuf, erecting a tent roughly 50 metres from residents' homes. **Read Zena Tahhan 's on-the-ground report from the occupied West Bank, which covers the attacks, the military raids, and the rapid expansion of illegal settler outposts [here](https://substack.com/redirect/fb0abd65-7da2-48fb-99ac-3cd03da30312?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**
* **Nablus:** Israeli settlers [uprooted](https://substack.com/redirect/1f488906-245d-4cb7-b4c1-7cef2c33e248?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) thousands of trees near Madama, southwest of Nablus, the village council's head reported.
* **Occupied East Jerusalem:** Israeli forces raided the UNRWA Qalandia Vocational Training Centre for the second time in less than a month on Monday, detaining dozens of students and staff inside the facility. Israeli forces also [arrested](https://substack.com/redirect/9107735f-baac-46c5-bc91-d053660594f8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the son of Jerusalem Governor, after raiding Silwan, south of Al-Aqsa Mosque, on Monday evening, the Palestinian Information Center reported.
* On Monday, Israeli forces [demolished](https://substack.com/redirect/12a8ce45-0727-42bf-892d-09e595eb9dbf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) four homes, 18 shops, two inhabited apartments and a livestock facility in Jenin, Ni'lin and occupied East Jerusalem.
* **Katz orders army takeover of another West Bank refugee camp:** Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz issued instructions to expand the scope of the military assault on the occupied West Bank and to prepare to occupy another Palestinian refugee camp under the model of the army invasions of the Jenin, Tulkarem, and Nur Shams camps in early 2025. According to Israeli [news outlets](https://substack.com/redirect/1b65ed94-f4dd-42d9-b984-f3d8544e93d1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Katz issued the order following a security assessment on Monday attended by military commanders and senior security and intelligence officials. Last year, Human Rights Watch [found](https://substack.com/redirect/ea2e91ae-03f7-44ad-8219-a10348f632a2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Israel's forced displacement of over 30,000 residents of the three refugee camps in the northern West Bank amounted to war crimes and crimes against humanity.
* **Sixty Palestinian prisoners released to Gaza, many showing signs of abuse:** Israel [released](https://substack.com/redirect/9467cfd2-be39-4134-9502-99e329af4b8c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 60 battered Gaza prisoners on Monday after they had spent months in detention, with many showing signs of abuse. Red Cross teams transferred them through the Karam Abu Salem crossing to Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital for urgent medical examinations.
* The group included 40 Palestinians held under harsh conditions in the Negev desert prison and 20 Gaza workers arrested inside Israel after October 7.
* **Rescue teams salvage additional bodies from Gaza wreckage:** Rescue teams [recovered](https://substack.com/redirect/6c53c888-402a-4357-b888-2e002ec17b5c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the remains of 99 Palestinians from beneath a destroyed home belonging to the Abu Sharia and Al-Hasayna families in Gaza City's Sabra neighborhood on Monday.
* The building had been struck in multiple Israeli airstrikes, including in October 2023 and June 2025.
* Crews said recovery operations are severely constrained by the destruction and Israel's total ban on heavy machinery, with around 8,000 Palestinians still believed to be buried beneath rubble across Gaza.
* **Israeli soldiers remove U.S. citizens from home in West Bank assault:** Israeli soldiers [forced](https://substack.com/redirect/f75c73d8-821d-4b71-a8c8-a31854f97352?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) two U.S. citizens from their home in Turmus Ayya, in the occupied West Bank, so troops could use it as a lookout position, their son, Dr. Said Shukri, told Drop Site News.
* The home belongs to Dr. Hassan Said Shukri, a neurologist based in Syracuse, New York.
* Shukri said soldiers carrying M16s pointed a gun at his 61-year-old mother and gave his parents one hour to pack. He contacted the U.S. Embassy, which said it could do nothing and refused to contact the Israeli military.
* His parents have since returned after the soldiers abruptly left. "It is only because of the public pressure that they were able to return to their home," Shukri said. He said soldiers had occupied the neighboring family's home for four days before moving directly into his parents' house.
* **Gaza groundwater too polluted to drink:** Gaza's groundwater is becoming too salty and contaminated to drink, the Gaza Ministry of Health [said](https://substack.com/redirect/fc74b8f4-b299-41e7-a2fb-ecda956abe74?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Monday.
* Groundwater now contains an average of 3,588 mg of dissolved salts per liter, more than three times the level generally considered acceptable.
* 19% of municipal wells are bacterially contaminated and 40% are not effectively chlorinated, Gaza Health Ministry Director General said, noting that nearly half of reported diseases are now linked to unsafe water and environmental conditions.
* **Hamas delegation heads to Cairo:** A Hamas negotiating delegation [traveled](https://substack.com/redirect/b44c2070-496e-45ed-b773-e2348913b8aa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to Cairo on Tuesday to continue second-phase negotiations on the Gaza ceasefire agreement, senior Hamas official Basem Naim announced in a social media post.
* Naim said talks with mediators would focus on consolidating the ceasefire and implementing first-phase commitments, particularly Israel's humanitarian obligations, before moving to phase two of President Donald Trump's plan.

# Lebanon
* **Israel continues military operations in Lebanon despite "ceasefire":**
* An Israeli drone strike Tuesday [hit](https://substack.com/redirect/89febe78-2c85-40d9-a293-a1c7a47ff24b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a residential apartment in Nabatieh Al-Fawqa, in Nabatieh, setting it ablaze, according to Lebanon's National News Agency.
* Israeli forces also carried out a large demolition in the village of Al-Qusayr in the Marjayoun district.
* In Tyre, explosions continued to echo into the morning as Israeli forces carried out [demolitions](https://substack.com/redirect/6ba894f8-020d-4ac2-a8d8-28af4b6980e9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the villages of Majdal Zoun, Al-Mansouri, and areas of Bint Jbeil.

# U.S. News
* **Deported couple found bound, shot dead in Guatemala: Nixon** **Giovanni P erez Paz** and **Glendy Marisol Gonz alez de la Cruz **were found bound, gagged and [shot to death](https://substack.com/redirect/c1cf1a60-7447-4c9f-8b56-4ac7e0097601?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in a sugarcane field in southern Guatemala weeks after Gonzalez de la Cruz self-deported to join her husband, who ICE had deported from Missouri last year, according to St. Louis Public Radio.
* Their 14-month-old daughter was found crying beside her mother's body and is recovering from dehydration, according to the Guatemalan news outlet ABC Stereo.
* "I felt that they took the thing I wanted most," Paz's brother said. "I felt a huge pain because it was my brother, my sister-in-law--people that wanted to work, to fight."
* **McConnell says he won 't return to Senate this week:** Sen. **Mitch McConnell** , 84, who was hospitalized for six weeks following a fall at his Capitol Hill home last month, [said](https://substack.com/redirect/089b0219-f4e2-4c5e-97ea-e06bee54fa3c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Monday he won't return to the Senate this week or attend Kentucky's annual Fancy Farm picnic, an event he's attended for more than four decades. McConnell's extended absence has complicated Republicans' narrow Senate margin, particularly on the Appropriations Committee.
* **Venezuelan men sue U.S. aviation firms that flew them to notorious Salvadoran prison:** More than 230 Venezuelan men [expelled](https://substack.com/redirect/38310d76-84ee-444f-9188-b661fff12ade?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by the Trump administration to El Salvador last year are suing CSI Aviation and GlobalX, accusing the companies of helping carry out illegal "rendition flights" to the Cecot maximum-security prison, **Jos e Olivares** reports for The Guardian.
* The lawsuit says the firms transported the men despite a federal judge ordering the planes to return and despite knowing they faced a foreseeable risk of torture. The men were held for four months and reported beatings, sexual assault, pepper spray and rubber-bullet attacks.
* CSI, ICE's largest contractor, received $1.23 billion from the agency in 2025 and subcontracted the three flights to GlobalX.
* **Mamdani announces plan to use city grocery stores to relieve rising prices:** New York City Mayor **Zohran Mamdani** [unveiled](https://substack.com/redirect/4d7a7304-d277-4639-858c-a5049d1539b2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) plans on Monday to sell essential groceries at prices 30% below typical retail rates through five city-owned stores, one in each borough.
* The discount will cover all fresh produce, meat, and seafood, along with 20 pantry, dairy, and refrigerated staples, including milk, cheese, and bread. Prices will be set at the beginning of each month and remain fixed throughout it, with no income restrictions for shoppers.
* The city has allocated $70 million to develop the stores and will cover rent and property taxes, while private contractors operate them. The first is expected to open in Hunts Point in the Bronx by late 2027, followed by La Marqueta in East Harlem by 2029. All five are planned to open before Mamdani's term ends.
* The administration estimates the program could save an average household about $1,000 annually. The stores will not sell alcohol, cigarettes, lottery tickets, or hot food, partly to limit competition with neighborhood bodegas.
* **ICE arrests over 12,000 after tips from child migrant agency, Reuters finds:** More than 12,000 people, including unaccompanied migrant children's sponsors and household members, have been [arrested](https://substack.com/redirect/ce963d2a-2adc-40f3-9fe4-5b75076fa5e4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by ICE following tips from the Office of Refugee Resettlement since January 2025, according to internal government data reviewed by Reuters, which found ORR shared more than 460,000 "leads" with ICE during that period.
* Former ORR deputy director **Jen Smyers** said safeguards against such data sharing have been "completely reversed," and accused the administration of "weaponizing a child welfare program for the purposes of more deportations."
* **Six House members bought SpaceX stock days after IPO** : At least six House members or their immediate families [purchased](https://substack.com/redirect/291ebaa0-388f-4ba9-9a5e-dd65ab535e7d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) between roughly $83,000 and $245,000 in SpaceX shares within six days of the company's June 12 IPO, CNBC found, with five of the buyers serving on committees overseeing aspects of the company's business, including defense and AI.
* The trades, which include purchases by Reps. **William Timmons**(R-S.C.), **Jared Moskowitz**(D-Fla.) and **Gil Cisneros**(D-Calif.)**** themselves and by spouses or children of Reps. **John McGuire**(R-Va.)**,** **Dan Meuser**(R-Pa.),**** and **John James** (R-Mich.), come as the House passed legislation Wednesday restricting future individual stock trading by lawmakers, though critics have pointed out the measure's weaknesses, including its non-extension to current holdings.
* **ACLU: LA immigration agents used racial slurs, targeted Latinos in raids** : Body camera footage and text messages [obtained](https://substack.com/redirect/01a15352-1b72-4322-b893-8f44d13190d7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) through court discovery show ICE and Border Patrol agents in Los Angeles using slurs like "tonk" and "wet" to refer to Latinos, according to a 42-page motion filed Monday by the ACLU.
* The filing argues evidence "flatly disproves" government claims that stops were based on intelligence rather than race, describing a shift toward mass "collateral" arrests through "roving patrols" at locations like Home Depots and car washes, and asks a federal judge to bar agents from relying on perceived Latino ethnicity to conduct stops.
* **Valdez endorses Lawrence: Claire Valdez** , who recently won a Democratic primary in New York's 7th district, endorsed progressive **William Lawrence** in his Michigan primary on Monday.
* **Moskowitz refuses to debate Larkin:** Rep. **Jared Moskowitz** has [pulled out](https://substack.com/redirect/05e377d2-2f7d-434b-a64c-65534c8619cf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of Monday night's debate with progressive challenger **Oliver Larkin** , hosted jointly by the Broward and Miami-Dade Democratic Black Caucuses.
* Larkin said he would still attend to address voters directly, declaring that he will be "debating an empty lectern."
* His campaign accused Moskowitz of avoiding scrutiny of his voting record and noted that the incumbent has not held a town hall in Florida's newly redrawn 25th Congressional District.
* **Michigan Senate debate: Abdul El-Sayed** and Rep. **Haley Stevens** went head-to-head in a debate on Monday night, with both candidates vying for the Democratic nomination for the open Senate seat in Michigan. The primary is next Tuesday, August 4.
* El-Sayed pointed out the $60 million in outside spending backing Stevens' campaign, saying she has been "bought off" by corporations that "expect to own your next U.S. senator."
* Abdul El-Sayed also blasted the record $46 million in AIPAC money backing Haley Stevens, saying it was spent because "they know she'll be a reliable vote," pointing to her vote last week for another $3.3 billion in aid to Israel.
* More highlights from the debate are available on our X feed,**[ here](https://substack.com/redirect/0915fe33-2fd0-4031-84ea-4a550a0f2305?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**

# Other International News
* **Fresh clashes erupt in Pakistan-administered Kashmir:** Clashes [broke out](https://substack.com/redirect/b03fd054-536d-4a8a-8cb9-308f6ec1619d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Monday in Rawalakot, Pakistan-administered Kashmir, as thousands of supporters of the Joint Awami Action Committee tried to march toward regional capital Muzaffarabad, part of weeks of protests demanding electoral reform ahead of a three-phase regional election that began the same day.
* The protests have called for the reallocation of parliamentary seats reserved for Kashmiris living elsewhere in Pakistan to those actually living in Azad Kashmir.
* The J.A.A.C. claimed several of their supporters died in clashes with police, though the deaths could not be confirmed as of Tuesday, bringing the reported death toll since protests began in early June to at least 30.
* **Dozens killed in air strikes on North Kordofan civilian sites** : Dozens of civilians were killed across a series of air strikes in Sudan's North Kordofan state between July 24 and 26, according to the rights group Emergency Lawyers, which reported drone attacks on a water station, a civilian vehicle, and a water well, health center and school, along with a bombing of a fuel-carrying vehicle in Um Badr. The strikes coincided with an escalation in clashes following an army ground offensive that cleared Rapid Support Forces from key routes.
* **At least 30 killed in armed attack on Nigerian village:** Gunmen [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/115db846-3692-4a42-aca8-d831d5fe89ff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at least 30 people, including eight children, in a nighttime raid on Naridon village in Nigeria's Kaduna state early Monday, residents told Reuters.
* A local leader said attackers opened fire on women, children and the elderly before setting houses ablaze and fleeing, with security personnel arriving only hours later.
* No group has claimed responsibility for the attack.
* **Keiko Fujimori sworn in as Peru 's president**: Keiko Fujimori is set to be [inaugurated](https://substack.com/redirect/d099697d-93fc-4283-a2e5-b25ccac7bc23?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) as Peru's president on Tuesday, becoming the country's 10th leader since 2016 after narrowly defeating leftist congressman Roberto Sanchez in June runoff election
* Fujimori, who has expressed interest in joining Trump's proposed "Shield of the Americas" regional security initiative, named former central bank board member Elmer Cuba as her economy minister on Tuesday, and Carlos Espa, a former U.S. embassy employee and presidential candidate, as her foreign minister.
* Fujimori inherits a fragmented, newly bicameral Congress where her Popular Force party holds the largest minority bloc.
* **Chad pulls out of ICC:** Chad [pulled out](https://substack.com/redirect/95d3369b-5763-4059-849e-2ab9d5eb5626?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of the ICC on Monday under U.S. pressure, complicating an ongoing probe into the genocide in Darfur.
* Chad's Foreign Ministry said on Monday it had notified the UN secretary-general of its decision to withdraw from the Rome Statute, the treaty underpinning the International Criminal Court, calling the court's record "limited and uneven" and focused on Africa.
* Chad said the request came from Washington, and that the U.S. deputy secretary of state for African affairs had urged it to reconsider its membership in a phone call last Thursday.
* The withdrawal could shield actors in the war in neighboring Darfur, where the U.S. and a UN fact-finding mission have both found the RSF committed genocide against non-Arab communities. Chad has been accused of serving as a conduit for arms reaching the RSF from the UAE.
* Chad is the fifth country to move toward withdrawal in recent months, after Venezuela on Friday and the September exit by Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger.
* **White phosphorus leak triggers brief evacuation near U.S. base in South Korea** : South Korean authorities briefly [ordered](https://substack.com/redirect/b247659f-9846-445c-bf73-f11f16d67fd6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) residents living close to Osan Air Base in Pyeongtaek, near Seoul, to evacuate Tuesday following a reported white phosphorus leak detected around 5 p.m., lifting the order hours later after decontamination was completed, the AP reported.
* The U.S. 51st Fighter Wing did not confirm a phosphorus leak but said it established a 1,000-foot safety cordon "due to a ground mishap and out of an abundance of caution," denying reports of a general base evacuation.
* **Afghan provincial official assassinated in Badakhshan** : Zabihullah Amiri, director of Badakhshan's Information and Culture Department, was [assassinated](https://substack.com/redirect/f777b825-9d82-4f84-b150-ea298db8e080?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Tuesday by two armed attackers near provincial capital Fayzabad, Afghanistan's Interior Ministry said.
* Amiri's guards killed one suspected attacker in a shootout while a search for the second continued. The ministry did not attribute blame to any specific group.
