This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Iran Attacks reported in Iraqi Kurdistan: Iranian forces reportedly a wave of drones toward Iraq's Kurdistan Region on Monday night, with repeated explosions and interceptions reported over Erbil. Kurdish journalist Scharo Bajalan reported at least two impacts: one in the Alana Valley near Soran, where a Komala opposition camp is located, and another north of Erbil. He said drones were launched from both Iran and areas controlled by Iraq's Popular Mobilization Forces. Footage circulating online appeared to show U.S. forces intercepting at least one drone over Erbil. The extent of any casualties or damage remains unclear. Explosions reported in Saudi Arabia; drone attacks on Jordan: Explosions were in eastern Saudi Arabia and drones attacked Jordan overnight, an Iranian state-linked outlet reported on Tuesday. At least 6 "powerful explosions" struck the eastern region of Saudi Arabia near oil and gas facilities, Nour News, an outlet affiliated with Iran's Supreme National Security Council, reported early Tuesday. The Saudi government has not confirmed the attack In a separate report, the outlet said local sources had described "extensive" drone attacks in the eastern desert of Jordan. Jordan's military said it shot down a drone that entered its airspace over the eastern desert near the borders with Iraq and Saudi Arabia early Tuesday, without identifying its origin. Separately, the Israeli military said it intercepted a drone near the Jordanian border that did not enter Israeli airspace and that it was investigating where it was launched from. Hormuz talks continue as Oman reportedly puts forward joint management proposal: Iran, Oman, and Gulf states stepped up diplomatic efforts over the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi separate phone calls with Oman's Badr Albusaidi and Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud. According to IRNA, the ministers reviewed regional developments and stressed strengthening diplomatic cooperation to restore stability and address "insecurity" in the Strait. Oman Iran with a proposal for a joint regional mechanism to manage the Strait of Hormuz with voluntary user fees, Reuters reported. Under the proposal, which reportedly has regional backing, Iran would no longer exercise sole control over the waterway. Foreign ministers from Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries also a virtual meeting on the ongoing U.S.-Iran negotiations on Tuesday. Oman's Foreign Ministry said they stressed the need for closer coordination on freedom and safety of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz while prioritising political and diplomatic solutions to strengthen regional security and stability. Iranian FM spokesperson discusses U.S. "quagmire": Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei to reporters on Monday about the U.S.' current position, saying that he did not believe they were "managing" the conflict well. "This war was supposed to force Iran to surrender," he said "but five months later they remain trapped in a quagmire." Baghaei reaffirmed that Iran would "not allow the United States to decide when war and peace begin and end." The spokesperson also Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who announced actions this weekend against Russian ships he claimed were being used to transport supplies to Iran. Baghaei compared Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky's conduct to anarchists who carried out dramatic and dangerous acts before World War I, calling his actions "theatrical" and saying that they "exaggerated" his "limited weight in international affairs." "Zelenskyy's patrons must rein him in," he said. Trump says that talks with Iran are "ongoing": President Donald Trump reporters on Air Force One on Monday that the U.S. was in "very deep talks" with Iran, and that there was a "good chance" of reaching an agreement, but that military action could resume if no deal is reached, saying that the U.S. would "go back to what we were doing two days ago." Neither Tehran nor Washington acknowledged any direct meetings, but indirect talks primarily involving Iran and Oman, and secondarily involving Qatar, Pakistan, Egypt, and U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, reportedly remain ongoing, according to Axios. The current negotiations are focused on reopening the Strait of Hormuz and restarting talks on a comprehensive nuclear agreement, according to the outlet. Trump also that the U.S. had "taken in billions and billions of dollars from Venezuela," and threatened that he would do the same with Iran. The comments follow reporting from the Financial Times last week that of the $13 billion in oil revenue seized by the U.S., $7 billion remains unaccounted for. When asked about this by reporters on Monday, he said the money he was being used to "run the country." Shipping remains severely constrained in Hormuz and Babl-Mandab: Windward seven Strait of Hormuz crossings on July 27, two of these inbound and five of them outbound, all using the northern Iran-run corridor. 14 vessels entered the Red Sea through the Bab Al-Mandab and 21 exited on July 26, Windward reported. Inbound traffic into the strait has collapsed by nearly 70%, and outbound traffic has fallen about 28%. Two more executed in Iran: Iran executed two men convicted on charges of killing police officers and damaging public properties during the mass protests in January, according to the state affiliated agency Mizan. The two men were identified as Abolfazl Sepahi Badjani and Amir Hossein Safari Hosseinabadi. Iran hanged two other men convicted in the same case earlier in July. Iran has executed dozens of people so far in 2026. Yemen Ansarallah claims strike on major Saudi oil facility in Abqaiq: Ansarallah responsibility on Monday for a drone strike on Saudi Aramco's Abqaiq crude-processing facility, the kingdom's largest. Abqaiq stabilizes the bulk of Saudi crude before export, making it one of the most critical nodes in the kingdom's oil infrastructure. It was also the target of the September 2019 drone and missile attack that briefly cut roughly 5% of global oil supply, causing a major shock in oil prices. Saudi Arabia's foreign ministry confirmed the attack, but attributed it to Iran-backed militias operating in Iraq. Ali Faleh al-Zaidi, Iraq's prime minister, security agencies to investigate Saudi Arabia's claim, according to the Iraqi News Agency. The Iraqi government said it would be examining the evidence and would pursue legal action against anyone found to have been involved Saudi Aramco shuts down Jazan refinery after Ansarallah attack: Saudi Aramco shut down its 400,000-barrel-per-day Jazan refinery following an Ansarallah attack, Reuters reported, citing consultancy IR. The attack reportedly damaged the refinery's integrated gasification combined-cycle (IGCC) complex and oil tank area, with repairs expected to allow an initial restart by August 15. Palestine Killed and wounded in Gaza: Over the past 24 hours, four Palestinians were killed--three in new attacks and one due to wounds sustained in earlier attacks--and 14 were injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,333 killed, with 174,023 injured. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,207 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 3,914, while 803 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble. Israel attacks Gaza on Monday and Tuesday: Israeli forces three Palestinians and wounded several others on Monday, shelling the northern and central parts of the Strip, according to Felesteen Online. An Israeli drone attack on Monday also wounded three fishermen near the Gaza port gate. An Israeli military vehicle on Deir-al-Balah on Tuesday, wounding two Palestinians, according to WAFA. At least eight Palestinians killed since Thursday as Israeli raids and settler attacks escalate across the occupied West Bank: Israeli forces and armed settlers continue to intensify their attacks across the occupied West Bank following Friday's settler attack in Tal. At least eight Palestinians, including a child, have been since Thursday, the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs reported. On Tuesday, raids, assaults, land seizures, and settler violence were reported across multiple governorates, according to WAFA, with at least 22 Palestinians detained by Israeli forces, according to the Palestinian Prisoners' Affairs office. Bethlehem: A Palestinian was after Israeli settlers beat him with an iron pipe near Al-Minya village. Israeli forces separately raided Tuqu' and Husan. Ramallah: Israeli forces Shuqba, west of Ramallah, on Tuesday morning and demolished a residential building, leaving the families who lived there homeless. Hebron: Israeli settlers Palestinians in the Khallet Al-Hamam area of Yatta, beating residents and firing tear gas. Israeli forces arrested a Palestinian father and his two sons after the attack. Forces also demolished two residential buildings. A Palestinian man in Masafer Yatta a weapon from a violent Israeli settler on Tuesday, becoming the third to attempt to do so in the last four days. Salfit: Israeli settlers a new settlement outpost on Palestinian land in Yasuf, erecting a tent roughly 50 metres from residents' homes. Read Zena Tahhan 's on-the-ground report from the occupied West Bank, which covers the attacks, the military raids, and the rapid expansion of illegal settler outposts . Nablus: Israeli settlers thousands of trees near Madama, southwest of Nablus, the village council's head reported. Occupied East Jerusalem: Israeli forces raided the UNRWA Qalandia Vocational Training Centre for the second time in less than a month on Monday, detaining dozens of students and staff inside the facility. Israeli forces also the son of Jerusalem Governor, after raiding Silwan, south of Al-Aqsa Mosque, on Monday evening, the Palestinian Information Center reported. On Monday, Israeli forces four homes, 18 shops, two inhabited apartments and a livestock facility in Jenin, Ni'lin and occupied East Jerusalem. Katz orders army takeover of another West Bank refugee camp: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz issued instructions to expand the scope of the military assault on the occupied West Bank and to prepare to occupy another Palestinian refugee camp under the model of the army invasions of the Jenin, Tulkarem, and Nur Shams camps in early 2025. According to Israeli , Katz issued the order following a security assessment on Monday attended by military commanders and senior security and intelligence officials. Last year, Human Rights Watch that Israel's forced displacement of over 30,000 residents of the three refugee camps in the northern West Bank amounted to war crimes and crimes against humanity. Sixty Palestinian prisoners released to Gaza, many showing signs of abuse: Israel 60 battered Gaza prisoners on Monday after they had spent months in detention, with many showing signs of abuse. Red Cross teams transferred them through the Karam Abu Salem crossing to Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital for urgent medical examinations. The group included 40 Palestinians held under harsh conditions in the Negev desert prison and 20 Gaza workers arrested inside Israel after October 7. Rescue teams salvage additional bodies from Gaza wreckage: Rescue teams the remains of 99 Palestinians from beneath a destroyed home belonging to the Abu Sharia and Al-Hasayna families in Gaza City's Sabra neighborhood on Monday. The building had been struck in multiple Israeli airstrikes, including in October 2023 and June 2025. Crews said recovery operations are severely constrained by the destruction and Israel's total ban on heavy machinery, with around 8,000 Palestinians still believed to be buried beneath rubble across Gaza. Israeli soldiers remove U.S. citizens from home in West Bank assault: Israeli soldiers two U.S. citizens from their home in Turmus Ayya, in the occupied West Bank, so troops could use it as a lookout position, their son, Dr. Said Shukri, told Drop Site News. The home belongs to Dr. Hassan Said Shukri, a neurologist based in Syracuse, New York. Shukri said soldiers carrying M16s pointed a gun at his 61-year-old mother and gave his parents one hour to pack. He contacted the U.S. Embassy, which said it could do nothing and refused to contact the Israeli military. His parents have since returned after the soldiers abruptly left. "It is only because of the public pressure that they were able to return to their home," Shukri said. He said soldiers had occupied the neighboring family's home for four days before moving directly into his parents' house. Gaza groundwater too polluted to drink: Gaza's groundwater is becoming too salty and contaminated to drink, the Gaza Ministry of Health on Monday. Groundwater now contains an average of 3,588 mg of dissolved salts per liter, more than three times the level generally considered acceptable. 19% of municipal wells are bacterially contaminated and 40% are not effectively chlorinated, Gaza Health Ministry Director General said, noting that nearly half of reported diseases are now linked to unsafe water and environmental conditions. Hamas delegation heads to Cairo: A Hamas negotiating delegation to Cairo on Tuesday to continue second-phase negotiations on the Gaza ceasefire agreement, senior Hamas official Basem Naim announced in a social media post. Naim said talks with mediators would focus on consolidating the ceasefire and implementing first-phase commitments, particularly Israel's humanitarian obligations, before moving to phase two of President Donald Trump's plan. Lebanon Israel continues military operations in Lebanon despite "ceasefire": An Israeli drone strike Tuesday a residential apartment in Nabatieh Al-Fawqa, in Nabatieh, setting it ablaze, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. Israeli forces also carried out a large demolition in the village of Al-Qusayr in the Marjayoun district. In Tyre, explosions continued to echo into the morning as Israeli forces carried out in the villages of Majdal Zoun, Al-Mansouri, and areas of Bint Jbeil. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com U.S. News Deported couple found bound, shot dead in Guatemala: Nixon Giovanni P erez Paz and Glendy Marisol Gonz alez de la Cruz were found bound, gagged and in a sugarcane field in southern Guatemala weeks after Gonzalez de la Cruz self-deported to join her husband, who ICE had deported from Missouri last year, according to St. Louis Public Radio. Their 14-month-old daughter was found crying beside her mother's body and is recovering from dehydration, according to the Guatemalan news outlet ABC Stereo. "I felt that they took the thing I wanted most," Paz's brother said. "I felt a huge pain because it was my brother, my sister-in-law--people that wanted to work, to fight." McConnell says he won 't return to Senate this week: Sen. Mitch McConnell , 84, who was hospitalized for six weeks following a fall at his Capitol Hill home last month, Monday he won't return to the Senate this week or attend Kentucky's annual Fancy Farm picnic, an event he's attended for more than four decades. McConnell's extended absence has complicated Republicans' narrow Senate margin, particularly on the Appropriations Committee. Venezuelan men sue U.S. aviation firms that flew them to notorious Salvadoran prison: More than 230 Venezuelan men by the Trump administration to El Salvador last year are suing CSI Aviation and GlobalX, accusing the companies of helping carry out illegal "rendition flights" to the Cecot maximum-security prison, Jos e Olivares reports for The Guardian. The lawsuit says the firms transported the men despite a federal judge ordering the planes to return and despite knowing they faced a foreseeable risk of torture. The men were held for four months and reported beatings, sexual assault, pepper spray and rubber-bullet attacks. CSI, ICE's largest contractor, received $1.23 billion from the agency in 2025 and subcontracted the three flights to GlobalX. Mamdani announces plan to use city grocery stores to relieve rising prices: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani plans on Monday to sell essential groceries at prices 30% below typical retail rates through five city-owned stores, one in each borough. The discount will cover all fresh produce, meat, and seafood, along with 20 pantry, dairy, and refrigerated staples, including milk, cheese, and bread. Prices will be set at the beginning of each month and remain fixed throughout it, with no income restrictions for shoppers. The city has allocated $70 million to develop the stores and will cover rent and property taxes, while private contractors operate them. The first is expected to open in Hunts Point in the Bronx by late 2027, followed by La Marqueta in East Harlem by 2029. All five are planned to open before Mamdani's term ends. The administration estimates the program could save an average household about $1,000 annually. The stores will not sell alcohol, cigarettes, lottery tickets, or hot food, partly to limit competition with neighborhood bodegas. ICE arrests over 12,000 after tips from child migrant agency, Reuters finds: More than 12,000 people, including unaccompanied migrant children's sponsors and household members, have been by ICE following tips from the Office of Refugee Resettlement since January 2025, according to internal government data reviewed by Reuters, which found ORR shared more than 460,000 "leads" with ICE during that period. Former ORR deputy director Jen Smyers said safeguards against such data sharing have been "completely reversed," and accused the administration of "weaponizing a child welfare program for the purposes of more deportations." Six House members bought SpaceX stock days after IPO : At least six House members or their immediate families between roughly $83,000 and $245,000 in SpaceX shares within six days of the company's June 12 IPO, CNBC found, with five of the buyers serving on committees overseeing aspects of the company's business, including defense and AI. The trades, which include purchases by Reps. William Timmons(R-S.C.), Jared Moskowitz(D-Fla.) and Gil Cisneros(D-Calif.)** themselves and by spouses or children of Reps. John McGuire(R-Va.), Dan Meuser(R-Pa.), and John James (R-Mich.), come as the House passed legislation Wednesday restricting future individual stock trading by lawmakers, though critics have pointed out the measure's weaknesses, including its non-extension to current holdings. ACLU: LA immigration agents used racial slurs, targeted Latinos in raids : Body camera footage and text messages through court discovery show ICE and Border Patrol agents in Los Angeles using slurs like "tonk" and "wet" to refer to Latinos, according to a 42-page motion filed Monday by the ACLU. The filing argues evidence "flatly disproves" government claims that stops were based on intelligence rather than race, describing a shift toward mass "collateral" arrests through "roving patrols" at locations like Home Depots and car washes, and asks a federal judge to bar agents from relying on perceived Latino ethnicity to conduct stops. Valdez endorses Lawrence: Claire Valdez , who recently won a Democratic primary in New York's 7th district, endorsed progressive William Lawrence in his Michigan primary on Monday. Moskowitz refuses to debate Larkin: Rep. Jared Moskowitz has of Monday night's debate with progressive challenger Oliver Larkin , hosted jointly by the Broward and Miami-Dade Democratic Black Caucuses. Larkin said he would still attend to address voters directly, declaring that he will be "debating an empty lectern." His campaign accused Moskowitz of avoiding scrutiny of his voting record and noted that the incumbent has not held a town hall in Florida's newly redrawn 25th Congressional District. Michigan Senate debate: Abdul El-Sayed and Rep. Haley Stevens went head-to-head in a debate on Monday night, with both candidates vying for the Democratic nomination for the open Senate seat in Michigan. The primary is next Tuesday, August 4. El-Sayed pointed out the $60 million in outside spending backing Stevens' campaign, saying she has been "bought off" by corporations that "expect to own your next U.S. senator." Abdul El-Sayed also blasted the record $46 million in AIPAC money backing Haley Stevens, saying it was spent because "they know she'll be a reliable vote," pointing to her vote last week for another $3.3 billion in aid to Israel. More highlights from the debate are available on our X feed,. Other International News Fresh clashes erupt in Pakistan-administered Kashmir: Clashes Monday in Rawalakot, Pakistan-administered Kashmir, as thousands of supporters of the Joint Awami Action Committee tried to march toward regional capital Muzaffarabad, part of weeks of protests demanding electoral reform ahead of a three-phase regional election that began the same day. The protests have called for the reallocation of parliamentary seats reserved for Kashmiris living elsewhere in Pakistan to those actually living in Azad Kashmir. The J.A.A.C. claimed several of their supporters died in clashes with police, though the deaths could not be confirmed as of Tuesday, bringing the reported death toll since protests began in early June to at least 30. Dozens killed in air strikes on North Kordofan civilian sites : Dozens of civilians were killed across a series of air strikes in Sudan's North Kordofan state between July 24 and 26, according to the rights group Emergency Lawyers, which reported drone attacks on a water station, a civilian vehicle, and a water well, health center and school, along with a bombing of a fuel-carrying vehicle in Um Badr. The strikes coincided with an escalation in clashes following an army ground offensive that cleared Rapid Support Forces from key routes. At least 30 killed in armed attack on Nigerian village: Gunmen at least 30 people, including eight children, in a nighttime raid on Naridon village in Nigeria's Kaduna state early Monday, residents told Reuters. A local leader said attackers opened fire on women, children and the elderly before setting houses ablaze and fleeing, with security personnel arriving only hours later. No group has claimed responsibility for the attack. Keiko Fujimori sworn in as Peru 's president: Keiko Fujimori is set to be as Peru's president on Tuesday, becoming the country's 10th leader since 2016 after narrowly defeating leftist congressman Roberto Sanchez in June runoff election Fujimori, who has expressed interest in joining Trump's proposed "Shield of the Americas" regional security initiative, named former central bank board member Elmer Cuba as her economy minister on Tuesday, and Carlos Espa, a former U.S. embassy employee and presidential candidate, as her foreign minister. Fujimori inherits a fragmented, newly bicameral Congress where her Popular Force party holds the largest minority bloc. Chad pulls out of ICC: Chad of the ICC on Monday under U.S. pressure, complicating an ongoing probe into the genocide in Darfur. Chad's Foreign Ministry said on Monday it had notified the UN secretary-general of its decision to withdraw from the Rome Statute, the treaty underpinning the International Criminal Court, calling the court's record "limited and uneven" and focused on Africa. Chad said the request came from Washington, and that the U.S. deputy secretary of state for African affairs had urged it to reconsider its membership in a phone call last Thursday. The withdrawal could shield actors in the war in neighboring Darfur, where the U.S. and a UN fact-finding mission have both found the RSF committed genocide against non-Arab communities. Chad has been accused of serving as a conduit for arms reaching the RSF from the UAE. Chad is the fifth country to move toward withdrawal in recent months, after Venezuela on Friday and the September exit by Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger. White phosphorus leak triggers brief evacuation near U.S. base in South Korea : South Korean authorities briefly residents living close to Osan Air Base in Pyeongtaek, near Seoul, to evacuate Tuesday following a reported white phosphorus leak detected around 5 p.m., lifting the order hours later after decontamination was completed, the AP reported. The U.S. 51st Fighter Wing did not confirm a phosphorus leak but said it established a 1,000-foot safety cordon "due to a ground mishap and out of an abundance of caution," denying reports of a general base evacuation. Afghan provincial official assassinated in Badakhshan : Zabihullah Amiri, director of Badakhshan's Information and Culture Department, was Tuesday by two armed attackers near provincial capital Fayzabad, Afghanistan's Interior Ministry said. Amiri's guards killed one suspected attacker in a shootout while a search for the second continued. | | | Peter, A child who survived the earthquake in Venezuela may have lost everything else.Their parents. Their home. Every relative who might have taken them in. Now they have nowhere to sleep, nothing to eat, and no one left to protect them.**When a child has nowhere to turn, someone else will offer to take her somewhere.** **Too often, that someone is a trafficker, and they know exactly how to make the offer sound like help. **

They study the gaps left behind by disaster, and they move quickly, often faster than the systems built to protect children can respond. A shelter without enough staff. A registration process that hasn't caught up. A crowd of frightened families too overwhelmed to watch every child closely. These are the openings traffickers are trained to find.

My name is Eduardo Verastegui. I produced the film Sound of Freedom, and founded the **Sound of Freedom Foundation** because I believe, without reservation, that every child deserves to be safe, and **none of them are for sale.** Right now, we are working urgently with organizations on the ground in Venezuela. We are helping so that displaced children what they need most: food, water, and a safe place to be found before a trafficker finds them first.

A simple meal or a safe shelter can be the difference between a child staying protected and a child disappearing into a trafficking network. **This work depends on partners we trust deeply, and on donors willing to help fund what those partners cannot do alone. ****Every dollar helps close a gap a trafficker would otherwise use. **We are also funding direct efforts to stop the traffickers themselves, before they can take another child. clean_body: 3 weeks left to help stop this Displaced children with nowhere to turn are exactly who traffickers target. | | | | | | | | GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE | | | | Peter, A child who survived the earthquake in Venezuela may have lost everything else.Their parents. Their home. Every relative who might have taken them in. Now they have nowhere to sleep, nothing to eat, and no one left to protect them.When a child has nowhere to turn, someone else will offer to take her somewhere. Too often, that someone is a trafficker, and they know exactly how to make the offer sound like help. They study the gaps left behind by disaster, and they move quickly, often faster than the systems built to protect children can respond. A shelter without enough staff. A registration process that hasn't caught up. A crowd of frightened families too overwhelmed to watch every child closely. These are the openings traffickers are trained to find. My name is Eduardo Verastegui. I produced the film Sound of Freedom, and founded the Sound of Freedom Foundation because I believe, without reservation, that every child deserves to be safe, and none of them are for sale. Right now, we are working urgently with organizations on the ground in Venezuela. We are helping so that displaced children what they need most: food, water, and a safe place to be found before a trafficker finds them first. A simple meal or a safe shelter can be the difference between a child staying protected and a child disappearing into a trafficking network. This work depends on partners we trust deeply, and on donors willing to help fund what those partners cannot do alone. Every dollar helps close a gap a trafficker would otherwise use. We are also funding direct efforts to stop the traffickers themselves, before they can take another child. This means supporting the people working every day to identify and disrupt these networks on the ground. Often quietly and at real personal risk so fewer children ever go missing in the first place. subject: One Week Left. Let's Finish This Together.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY KAREN CRNKOVICH FOR JOHNSON COUNTY COMMISSION * 6709 West 119th Street * Ste
body:
One week from today, voters will make an important decision.

| | | | | |
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Friends,One week from today, voters will make an important decision.This primary will determine who goes head-to-head with Mike Kelly in November.If you believe Johnson County deserves new leadership, this election is your opportunity to choose the candidate best prepared to bring fiscal discipline, transparency, and accountability back to county government. But more importantly, choose the candidate ready and able to bring the fight to Mike Kelly.I stepped into this race because I believe our county is headed in the wrong direction. Property taxes continue to climb, bureaucracy continues to grow and too many residents feel like their voices are no longer being heard.I've spent my career outside of government, building a business, creating jobs, balancing budgets, and solving problems. I've also spent years serving our community through nonprofit leadership because I believe leadership is about serving others.That real-world, diverse experience is exactly what Johnson County needs.Over the past several months, I've traveled throughout our county listening to residents, answering tough questions, and sharing a clear vision for our future.
* A county government that lives within its means.
* Leadership that is transparent and accountable.
* Decisions based on common sense, not politics.

A commitment to protecting what makes Johnson County one of the best places in America to live, work, and raise a family.Now, I need your help.**If you haven't voted yet, please make your plan today. Vote early or vote on Election Day, but most importantly, vote.**[**Advanced Voting Locations**](https://us.list-manage.com/PRsNtkvNHsd?e=7320325a61&c2id=7adf4106091b2bdf32986c5b36d3a494)[**Election Day Location Finder**](https://us.list-manage.com/Ym43FwxHlvD?e=7320325a61&c2id=7adf4106091b2bdf32986c5b36d3a494) And if you believe I'm the strongest candidate to take on Mike Kelly this fall, please tell your friends, your family, and your neighbors._Elections like this are decided by turnout, and every vote matters._ Together, we can earn the opportunity to offer Johnson County a new direction this November.I'd be honored to earn your vote.Karen CrnkovichCandidate for Johnson County Commission Chair

| Peter,

[BREAKING NEWS: A federal judge just ruled that FDA restrictions on the abortion pill mifepristone are baseless.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/136153612/636525514/2141984067?sourceid=1151512&utm_campaign=27emama-0701aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=medab&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyOWRiZTY4Ny05ZDhhLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=b7UIyPQH45q5s2XPO4Ir0XUcVNWqS87MxH1i7JcO1bM=&emci=26dbe687-9d8a-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=29dbe687-9d8a-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=954237)

We filed the case, _Whole Woman's Health Alliance v. FDA_ , back in 2023 on behalf of abortion providers in Virginia, Kansas, and Montana. Three years later, we have a ruling [and your support helped make this victory possible.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/136153613/636525515/2141984067?sourceid=1151512&utm_campaign=27emama-0701aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=medab&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyOWRiZTY4Ny05ZDhhLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=b7UIyPQH45q5s2XPO4Ir0XUcVNWqS87MxH1i7JcO1bM=&emci=26dbe687-9d8a-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=29dbe687-9d8a-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=954237) | [Fund Our Lawsuits](https://click.everyaction.com/k/136153614/636525516/2141984067?sourceid=1151512&utm_campaign=27emama-0701aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=medab&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyOWRiZTY4Ny05ZDhhLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=b7UIyPQH45q5s2XPO4Ir0XUcVNWqS87MxH1i7JcO1bM=&emci=26dbe687-9d8a-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=29dbe687-9d8a-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=954237)
---
This ruling is a win for science. States and politicians target mifepristone for political reasons, not safety. [The court confirmed what we've always known: mifepristone is exceedingly safe.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/136153615/636525517/2141984067?sourceid=1151512&utm_campaign=27emama-0701aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=medab&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyOWRiZTY4Ny05ZDhhLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=b7UIyPQH45q5s2XPO4Ir0XUcVNWqS87MxH1i7JcO1bM=&emci=26dbe687-9d8a-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=29dbe687-9d8a-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=954237) This fight was never about science. It's about making abortion harder to access.

Mifepristone is one of the most-studied medications in America. More than 7.5 million people have used it safely since 2000. The FDA has confirmed this again and again for 25 years.

[None of that has stopped politicians from targeting it. But today's win shows your gift drives real change.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/136153616/636525518/2141984067?sourceid=1151512&utm_campaign=27emama-0701aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=medab&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyOWRiZTY4Ny05ZDhhLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=b7UIyPQH45q5s2XPO4Ir0XUcVNWqS87MxH1i7JcO1bM=&emci=26dbe687-9d8a-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=29dbe687-9d8a-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=954237)

Our win also is critical to counter the opposition. Right now, a separate abortion pills case about to be heard by the Fifth Circuit. In that case, Louisiana argues that mifepristone is too accessible—the opposite of what the court ruled in our case—and wants to block patients nationwide from getting their abortion pills by mail or at a pharmacy.

A quarter of all abortions in the U.S. now happen through telehealth—the Louisiana case could end that access. We, along with movement partners and providers, filed amicus briefs pointing out the realities of care and restrictions. Oral argument is set for September [and we need you with us.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/136153617/636525519/2141984067?sourceid=1151512&utm_campaign=27emama-0701aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=medab&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyOWRiZTY4Ny05ZDhhLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=b7UIyPQH45q5s2XPO4Ir0XUcVNWqS87MxH1i7JcO1bM=&emci=26dbe687-9d8a-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=29dbe687-9d8a-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=954237)

This is what the fight looks like right now: win in one courtroom, defend the win in another. [We won't stop—but we can't do it without you.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/136153618/636525520/2141984067?sourceid=1151512&utm_campaign=27emama-0701aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=medab&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyOWRiZTY4Ny05ZDhhLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=b7UIyPQH45q5s2XPO4Ir0XUcVNWqS87MxH1i7JcO1bM=&emci=26dbe687-9d8a-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=29dbe687-9d8a-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=954237)

clean_body: This ruling is a win for science | | | | | | Peter, We filed the case, Whole Woman's Health Alliance v. FDA , back in 2023 on behalf of abortion providers in Virginia, Kansas, and Montana. Three years later, we have a ruling | This ruling is a win for science. States and politicians target mifepristone for political reasons, not safety. This fight was never about science. It's about making abortion harder to access. Mifepristone is one of the most-studied medications in America. More than 7.5 million people have used it safely since 2000. The FDA has confirmed this again and again for 25 years. Our win also is critical to counter the opposition. Right now, a separate abortion pills case about to be heard by the Fifth Circuit. In that case, Louisiana argues that mifepristone is too accessible—the opposite of what the court ruled in our case—and wants to block patients nationwide from getting their abortion pills by mail or at a pharmacy. A quarter of all abortions in the U.S. now happen through telehealth—the Louisiana case could end that access. We, along with movement partners and providers, filed amicus briefs pointing out the realities of care and restrictions. Oral argument is set for September This is what the fight looks like right now: win in one courtroom, defend the win in another. Team,

We can't just be anti-Trump.

Opposing Trump is the easy part — everyone in our party agrees on that. But if we only offer people what we're against, we give them no reason to believe things will actually get better.

There's a reason the Democratic Party lost to Trump _twice_. Voters see the difference between someone who fights for them and someone who's just holding a seat. And after 20 years of the same representation in CA-07, a lot of people have stopped believing this party will fight for them at all.

I'm running to change that. So let me tell you what I'm actually for:

I'm for healthcare you don't have to go bankrupt to afford. Housing a working family can actually pay for. An end to the endless wars draining billions from our schools and neighborhoods. Protecting immigrant families instead of funding the agency that terrorizes them. And a government that answers to the people it serves — not the corporate donors writing the checks.

That last part is the whole thing. It's why I have never taken a dime from corporate PACs, and never will. When you don't owe anything to insurance companies, defense contractors, or big real estate, you're free to actually fight for working families.

**Doris Matsui can't say that. I can.**

That's exactly why corporate PACs and outside groups are lining up behind David Valadao. He's taken over $1.2 million from the healthcare industry alone, then cast the deciding vote to gut Medi-Cal for tens of thousands of families here in the Valley.

DEAR FRIENDS,

Right now, I'm being attacked by my primary opponent, the leadership of the Rhode Island Republican Party, and—of course—Seth
Magaziner.

They are questioning my loyalty to our country. They are claiming I am somehow undermining President Trump and Secretary of State
Marco Rubio.

These are the same people who, just a short time ago, said I was too MAGA. Too loyal to President Trump.

Now they want you to believe I am working against him.

They can't have it both ways.

These politicians are trying to manipulate Rhode Islanders.

From day one, I instructed my campaign to release everything openly and transparently so Rhode Islanders would have zero doubt
about my intentions. I have issued more press releases, made more public statements, and participated in more no-holds-barred
interviews on this issue. My critics either did not pay attention to them—or they chose to ignore them.

I do what I believe is right. I do what I believe is right for Rhode Island, not what is easy.

And when you do the right thing, you face criticism. You face attacks. That comes with bold leadership.

Here are the cold, hard facts...

Rhode Island is last in business, last in opportunity for our young adults. As national employment is booming, Rhode Island, under
its current leadership, is bleeding jobs—1,900 lost year to date—and we continue to lose employers. Think Hasbro.

I traveled to Cuba for humanitarian purposes. I visited churches and hospitals, delivering medical supplies and needed hygienic
products.

While I was there, an opportunity to meet with Cuban leadership developed organically. It was not the purpose of my trip.

I participated as a private American citizen—not as a representative of the United States government.

I have complete confidence in President Trump and Secretary Rubio. They have shown strength, discipline, and a clear commitment to
putting America's interests first. I did not speak for either of them. I did not speak for the United States government, the Cuban
government, or anyone else. I spoke only for myself, as a private American citizen.

I shared my perspective on free enterprise, economic reform, and the steps Cuba could take to create relationships with Rhode
Island businesses, after the Trump administration opens trade.

It's not lost on me, the history of Cuba and the struggles of the Cuban people. When President Trump says Cuba is next, I believe
him.

When trade with Cuba expands under United States policy, enormous investment will follow. When that happens, Rhode Island will be
in competition with 49 other states for those opportunities. In global trade, timing is everything. Somebody is going to win those
opportunities. Why not Rhode Island?

To ensure complete transparency, I filed the appropriate FARA documents and publicly disclosed the materials connected to those
conversations, including my peace-and-prosperity ideas based on decades of business experience. All of which, I was not
compensated for.

Those filings are public and speak for themselves. Filing under FARA is a disclosure to the United States government; it does not
mean that I represented the United States government or the Cuban Government.

I am

One hundred percent transparent.

One hundred percent lawful.

One hundred percent leadership.

Three weeks after my visit, Cuban leadership independently announced 176 reforms—Cuba's largest economic overhaul since 1959.

I am not claiming my visit caused those reforms.

I am saying I recognized that change was coming, I was willing to have a conversation, and I want Rhode Island businesses and
Rhode Island workers positioned to benefit when those markets open.

Seth Magaziner, how many jobs have you created as a private citizen, let alone as a politician?

[pause] I speak to Rhode Islanders every day, and i can assure you they feel how many jobs you have lost.

I served as a United States Marine and now I am Serving Rhode Island. My campaign has the most support, the best team, the best
Rhode Island Leaders and with the help of my fellow Rhode Islanders, I am here to defeat you.

Sincerely,

Vic Mellor

Candidate for Congress, Rhode Island's 2nd District

clean_body: [] LET'S TALK ABOUT CUBA [] [] DEAR FRIENDS, Right now, I'm being attacked by my primary opponent, the leadership of the Rhode Island Republican Party, and—of course—Seth Magaziner. They are questioning my loyalty to our country. They are claiming I am somehow undermining President Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio. These are the same people who, just a short time ago, said I was too MAGA. Too loyal to President Trump. Now they want you to believe I am working against him. They can't have it both ways. These politicians are trying to manipulate Rhode Islanders. From day one, I instructed my campaign to release everything openly and transparently so Rhode Islanders would have zero doubt about my intentions. I have issued more press releases, made more public statements, and participated in more no-holds-barred interviews on this issue. My critics either did not pay attention to them—or they chose to ignore them. I do what I believe is right. I do what I believe is right for Rhode Island, not what is easy. And when you do the right thing, you face criticism. You face attacks. That comes with bold leadership. Here are the cold, hard facts... Rhode Island is last in business, last in opportunity for our young adults. As national employment is booming, Rhode Island, under its current leadership, is bleeding jobs—1,900 lost year to date—and we continue to lose employers. Think Hasbro. I traveled to Cuba for humanitarian purposes. I visited churches and hospitals, delivering medical supplies and needed hygienic products. While I was there, an opportunity to meet with Cuban leadership developed organically. It was not the purpose of my trip. I participated as a private American citizen—not as a representative of the United States government. I have complete confidence in President Trump and Secretary Rubio. They have shown strength, discipline, and a clear commitment to putting America's interests first. I did not speak for either of them. I did not speak for the United States government, the Cuban government, or anyone else. I spoke only for myself, as a private American citizen. I shared my perspective on free enterprise, economic reform, and the steps Cuba could take to create relationships with Rhode Island businesses, after the Trump administration opens trade. It's not lost on me, the history of Cuba and the struggles of the Cuban people. When President Trump says Cuba is next, I believe him. When trade with Cuba expands under United States policy, enormous investment will follow. When that happens, Rhode Island will be in competition with 49 other states for those opportunities. In global trade, timing is everything. Somebody is going to win those opportunities. Why not Rhode Island? To ensure complete transparency, I filed the appropriate FARA documents and publicly disclosed the materials connected to those conversations, including my peace-and-prosperity ideas based on decades of business experience. All of which, I was not compensated for. Those filings are public and speak for themselves. Filing under FARA is a disclosure to the United States government; it does not mean that I represented the United States government or the Cuban Government. I am One hundred percent transparent. One hundred percent lawful. One hundred percent leadership. Three weeks after my visit, Cuban leadership independently announced 176 reforms—Cuba's largest economic overhaul since 1959. I am not claiming my visit caused those reforms. I am saying I recognized that change was coming, I was willing to have a conversation, and I want Rhode Island businesses and Rhode Island workers positioned to benefit when those markets open. Seth Magaziner, how many jobs have you created as a private citizen, let alone as a politician? [pause] I speak to Rhode Islanders every day, and i can assure you they feel how many jobs you have lost. I served as a United States Marine and now I am Serving Rhode Island. My campaign has the most support, the best team, the best Rhode Island Leaders and with the help of my fellow Rhode Islanders, I am here to defeat you. Sincerely, Vic Mellor Candidate for Congress, Rhode Island's 2nd District [] [] [] [] [] [] [] Want to change how you receive these emails?

clean_body: Bernie Sanders and Keith Ellison just rallied behind her. Here's what she said on stage. | Fellow Conservative - Bernie Sanders came to Minneapolis last week - on a private jet. He stood on a stage with Keith Ellison to rally support for Peggy Flanagan's campaign for the Senate. Peggy told the crowd she backs Medicare for All, universal child care, and a national paid leave mandate. Then she said this: she supports "ripping ICE apart..." Read that again. A candidate for the United States Senate wants to tear apart the agency that removes violent criminals from our communities. Fellow Conservative, I need you with me on this one. I spent 21 years as a Marine and a Navy SEAL fighting threats to this country overseas. Nine deployments. Over 70 countries. I didn't do that, so a Bernie Sanders-endorsed candidate could dismantle everything I fought to defend overseas from within our borders. I am proud of my service to our great nation and of my fight to defend our American way of life overseas. My promise to you is that I will continue the fight - this time at home. # _One Week To Go: Let's Finish Strong!_
---
| |
**We're officially one week away from Primary Election Day, and this is the moment we've been working toward. Every conversation, every door knocked, every phone call, and every volunteer shift has helped build the momentum that's carrying us into the final stretch.**
**Now it's time to bring that energy all the way to Election Day. Whether you've been with us since day one or are just getting involved, there's a place for you on Team Elizabeth during this final week! Together, we can make sure every supporter knows when, where, and how to vote.**
**Before we sprint through the last few days, let's take a moment to celebrate everything we've accomplished together.**

### Team Elizabeth Celebration
**Join us this Friday for an evening celebrating the incredible volunteers, supporters, and friends who have powered this campaign. It's a chance to connect, recharge, and get excited for the final push.****Sign up below:**
---
| [Pre-Primary Celebration](https://us.list-manage.com/SEPRU9M3K_z?e=2f83c585b2&c2id=3b13c473c2db4883f0cc0c9f59510326)
---
| |

### Election Night Watch Party
**Then on Tuesday, join us for our Election Night Watch Party! We'll gather for some backyard fun, good food, and great company as we watch the results come in together. No matter what happens, we'll celebrate the hard work this team has put into this campaign and the community we've built along the way.****Sign up below:**
---
| [Election Night Watch Party](https://us.list-manage.com/DtZGIwpkUVR?e=2f83c585b2&c2id=3b13c473c2db4883f0cc0c9f59510326)
---
| |

## Help Us Welcome Voters at the Polls
**As voting begins to wrap up, one of the most important ways you can help is by serving as a poll greeter. Poll greeting is one of the most rewarding volunteer opportunities because you get to be the friendly face of our campaign as voters head into the polls. You'll greet neighbors, hand out campaign literature, answer basic questions, and help make sure Elizabeth is the last candidate voters hear about before they cast their ballots.****It's also a fantastic way to:**
* **Connect with your community and meet fellow voters.**
* **Build excitement and enthusiasm for the campaign.**
* **Encourage supporters to head into the polls with confidence.**
* **Help us collect valuable information that gives our team an early picture of how Election Day is unfolding.**

**Whether you've volunteered before or this would be your first time, we'll make sure you have everything you need to be successful.****Sign up to be a poll greeter below:**
---
| [Join The Poll Greeters!](https://us.list-manage.com/xA9bUSNDKeh?e=2f83c585b2&c2id=3b13c473c2db4883f0cc0c9f59510326)
---
| |

## Let's Finish This Together
**The final week of a campaign is powered by people who show up. Every shift matters. Every conversation matters. Every volunteer matters. Let's make these last seven days count, celebrate all we've accomplished, and leave everything on the field for Election Day.**
**We'll see you on the campaign trail—and then at the celebration!**

Derek,
I'm writing to ask you to [**chip in $7 to the DNC today**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-july-2026-gfr?refcode=em_20260728_8254_fr&amount=7&refcode2=8254_22930333_gBzLVR&akid=8254%2E22930333%2EgBzLVR) — but first, I want to explain why your support in this specific moment is so critical.
The truth is that we have a real shot at winning back control of the Senate this November. That would mean electing a majority that can really put a check on the Trump administration and stick up for the interests of working Americans, not billionaires.

subject: 🚨 The CDC just crossed a dangerous line.

As a microbiologist, I never imagined I would open the CDC's website and see it cast doubt on one of the most well-established findings in modern medicine. But after Donald Trump put Robert F. Kennedy Jr. in charge of our nation's public health system, I guess I shouldn't be surprised.
The CDC recently changed its "Autism and Vaccines" page to state: "The claim vaccines do not cause autism is not an evidence-based claim." This is an alarming change—it sends a dangerous message to parents who deserve facts, not politics.
What troubles me even more is that this wasn't driven by a breakthrough in scientific research. The evidence didn't suddenly change overnight.
Instead, reports indicate that the language became part of negotiations to confirm the next CDC Director. Think about that for a moment. The words on one of the world's once-most-trusted public health websites were changed as part of a political deal.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em?]
You don't negotiate science. You don't base scientific findings on what is politically convenient. Public health isn't supposed to work that way.
What makes this even more frustrating is that our public health leaders have real problems demanding their attention. Right now, we're dealing with foodborne illness outbreaks and other serious health threats that require clear communication and public confidence. Instead of focusing on those challenges, RFK Jr. is reopening a conspiracy theory that has already been answered by decades of research.
I've spent my career studying infectious diseases and teaching the next generation of scientists. I know what happens when we stop trusting evidence and start letting politics dictate science. It doesn't end with one webpage. It affects vaccination rates, public confidence, and ultimately the health of our communities.
That's why I'm running to be the first microbiologist in Congress.
We need more scientists in elected office and fewer politicians willing to gamble with public health. If you believe facts still matter and that Georgia deserves leaders who will stand up for science no matter who's in the White House, I'm asking for your support today. Will you chip in $15 to help me fight for evidence, public health, and the truth? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em?]
DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em?]
Thank you for standing with science.
— Dr. Jasmine Clark

| | Fellow Conservative, If you haven’t heard about “See You at the Library Day” on Fox News or Newsmax or your other favorite news sources, _**[please let me tell you why it’s so critical.](http://links.freedomfirstalert.com/u/click?_t=9ca143e971904d26a973d002cb0ae7f7&_m=0c92ad71489040ce9b3f711089613f96&_e=QnD8UAIUR3ej-qtJmNDUuETBrt8yS5MpM8F8OaE6kP7dC0NthOTcDKcWWk9KaH1mlj7xv7ZEBSEe8gWiFaQdI0lVFekZMrF4uFRMcTnX2GxHhjbmhiyAoOthJPJq4j3FlBHoleFjjCzYUXAseXiAap62lqlfjfW0zQvKkVrYjOYFswX82_FmGeiPnOwIixwiMcMHSFByw0m6xHSyXH5R1J3YT2BkxGN8yeEjWin6H2RnDcmn3peLMBC-P8oXh7FgUZ1EbOGKYqIkiNwXQmJOt1WNElv_o41qIPZxsLZSWjZHhR1trZwHpVv0x84eXIEZbBzq1WNkJ-TDdt5bdQaYaX8wuzwi-ROTS9LGRWcllGhuBax7YLMKIoT8RPJCEfg6mOVslDxNEnvYCALfY5TdL4VudL3xFKvCtBakp6kSnFfJIZ2-yfBWt4yRm2qVyesMVqsB6UGb3OrmSg7n44MTa9GS157AboOEz9UemGnMmiK6tFxEXMUR9c_h6_UwuREsO46jffndf1Kj8OqeQHtXHxKJny4MfamGGovWQ3QlUnWL6XnaCgae8oJFur5BK5Qt15GZq_lj0BDK2Keph8pd_K89eNUMlpqvk9FTRCIE-L0nfs6wEzMRUtVs_-5mEvrCwibY2h-kDwsAGkw6lLi9oQZ8J1OvtKm5P9Ejx54AJBGzFCxTEmzoMXlBpyqEOavY3roVOj1K-Kn1HTDBuseoJLret4CSd8TQNGRKR2twK-I%3D)**_ Back when you were growing up, you may remember lazy Saturdays at the library with a kind but stern librarian.She would fill your mind with classics like _Pat the Bunny_ and _The Little Engine That Could_. And eventually you got old enough to roam by yourself and discover adventures like the _Three Musketeers_ , _Treasure Island_ and _Charlotte’s Web_.But today, all that has changed. Instead of filling children with wholesome stories, the president of the American Library Association (ALA) says libraries should be used to address ‘systemic racism’ and elevate ‘BIPOC and GLBTQR+ writers and voices.’ Radical librarians call _Adventures of Huckleberry Finn_ and _To Kill a Mockingbird_ “racist.” They’ve stripped Laura Ingalls Wilder’s name from a prestigious book award because of her “problematic’ _Little House_ series.And they bring in men wearing full makeup, dresses, and high heels for “Drag Queen Story Hours” where books like these are read to children of all ages... _A is for Activist._ An _ABC_ _board_ _book_ for “families who want their kids to grow up in a space that is unapologetic about activism, environmental justice, civil rights, LGBTQ rights, and everything else that activists believe in and fight for.” _Woke Baby_. “For all the littlest progressives, waking up to seize a new day of justice and activism. Woke babies raise their fists in the air. Woke babies cry out for justice. Woke babies grow up to change the world.” _Prince and Knight._ The “premier queer-friendly fairy tale” about a prince who marries a knight instead of a princess. And _The Hips on the Drag Queens Go Swish, Swish, Swish._ A “family-friendly celebration of drag” that encourages children to “work it.”I wish I could tell you this was only happening in places like New York City and San Francisco...

| | _**[That’s why parents and grandparents across the country are rising up through See You At The Library Day.](http://links.freedomfirstalert.com/u/click?_t=9ca143e971904d26a973d002cb0ae7f7&_m=0c92ad71489040ce9b3f711089613f96&_e=QnD8UAIUR3ej-qtJmNDUuETBrt8yS5MpM8F8OaE6kP7dC0NthOTcDKcWWk9KaH1mlj7xv7ZEBSEe8gWiFaQdI0lVFekZMrF4uFRMcTnX2GxHhjbmhiyAoOthJPJq4j3FlBHoleFjjCzYUXAseXiAap62lqlfjfW0zQvKkVrYjOYFswX82_FmGeiPnOwIixwiMcMHSFByw0m6xHSyXH5R1J3YT2BkxGN8yeEjWin6H2RnDcmn3peLMBC-P8oXh7FgxLw6dxxKGYviUcQB7OdOrNnHLbiuBHqXSHuRXB1Lcfc55pw5bWGsJNfxkqwejROys3kpR0gNh5WxiZNvEZgjDJkeLFTkk3ulksQtV9FjhMCyA1OWRItyZ8R5II-pMAuvPNNlawCj-RN6ZOV6Hj6xuiBKlbpqwI9GWzx2OiRGiIJpeA93POu-aEiq-NPQ4J0DwxlLdHsyuFDiOW1MC6XZkBjsd-QM975TFHIxc0aC6IrEO7pUj-l_UuLyjKOm8GeaoszycdLlhNk44rWaYEvsnE3yBMXumryp-GHzQDFLH-uZJ8PFTiFm_uTa8dZEfHWg7x4i7pSRC-C5wl1K7sIQYxH-9UNaf59GfcO4wYZemNYH6XTm1EuqYp38oo6W9-xiow7zgWYQeZ1iFax6LBeIgkw7mjOTOC1SmqDgt9oC9Ua63EWsxZnOGwaD384RqI-6rE9WJGZMeboeUW1w8EXy0tVQjuymEMjg2QMN3F1QjCs%3D)**_ For decades, the ultra-liberal Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation and George Soros’ Open Society have spent millions radicalizing the ALA.And as a result, a new generation of pink-haired, activist librarians have made it their mission to fill library shelves with anti-American, LGBTQ-friendly, and explicitly sexual content.Maybe you’ve noticed all the displays at your own library celebrating Pride Month or elevating ‘the environment’ to a type of religion. Or maybe you’ve noticed the “Teen Zone” which is really meant to be a “parent-free” zone.The “Teen Zone” is filled with books like: _Rick_ about a cross-dressing Grandpa, _Melissa_ filled with graphic nudity, and _Darkstalker_ featuring gory violence and domestic abuse.But here’s what’s really alarming. We can’t just sit back and say, “Well, I’ll just make sure my family doesn’t go to “Drag Queen Story Hour” and we won’t check out those inappropriate books.”That may be good for your family -- for now.But meanwhile, the ALA uses our taxpayer-funded libraries to lure in millions of _other_ children who grow up to be the very activists who are destroying our country and conservative values!_**[I hope you see why I need your help today.](http://links.freedomfirstalert.com/u/click?_t=9ca143e971904d26a973d002cb0ae7f7&_m=0c92ad71489040ce9b3f711089613f96&_e=QnD8UAIUR3ej-qtJmNDUuETBrt8yS5MpM8F8OaE6kP7dC0NthOTcDKcWWk9KaH1mlj7xv7ZEBSEe8gWiFaQdI0lVFekZMrF4uFRMcTnX2GxHhjbmhiyAoOthJPJq4j3FlBHoleFjjCzYUXAseXiAap62lqlfjfW0zQvKkVrYjOYFswX82_FmGeiPnOwIixwiMcMHSFByw0m6xHSyXH5R1J3YT2BkxGN8yeEjWin6H2RnDcmn3peLMBC-P8oXh7Fg7CQWEzNX6H9Uu9vyF4mipP7eqmRxW9HXadetTT8z-Ii1DsY1f4ZV2DezdI2pt-_dPedL2IUXYs19ZafouYAHOdp-V89W_f3_3ePk-AmgVeS7U-195F8dG3p3qVF0ZziBFvW8u_GMlor5QVGFMK18mvz9nwf7XaqD52IJm_40v-w1brwb91V0S_7SyLJuw0NTfnoztFZ99JXD4FIw7wKYJbQxB8e67azS-tb1gYzcGeG9ZOf0FJSbtXYgxNAz5G-IK5lxWe9q3rrfZotYwfujkqXiNclH7Ki3pEOz0YR8rFSgqbNMoSdz287YUPfgj4VoJjZPhLNGuCeUqsp0s4223dTsdHJ1WKYIEaDwnjwk2MAb0nEDFvGGqiT3OlxWirIkQmL6vjKr_AijaDqjvAxQhVAyMBRlra5ofduBwOQ_Lrms5QzEUMCoJO1VP6ouqaIUrtiWa7ZJFrmO5MvaA6_0ikQQCJarIjYnyrbtbnSuSW8%3D) **_My name is Kirk Cameron. Hey friends,
**I’m thrilled to share with you episode 3 of the** _**Standing Tall**_**podcast!**
_****_
**
CLICK HERE:**[**LISTEN NOW**](https://us.list-manage.com/uSia8Ay6Afe?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)
Fifty years ago, Alex Haley's _Roots_ changed how this country understood its own history. This year, on the anniversary of that book, a Tennessee school district [banned it](https://us.list-manage.com/ZnPceBKbggS?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0) from library shelves — in the same city that has a 13-foot statue of Haley holding that very book.
**This week I sat down with Chris Haley (Alex Haley's great-nephew) and Bill Haley Jr. (his grandson, and a 9th-generation descendant of Kunta Kinte himself)** to talk about all of it — the cultural impact _Roots_ had in 1976, the recent ban and its reversal here in Knox County, and what it means that we're fighting some of these same battles again today. We also get into the upcoming [Roots 50th Commemorative Experience](https://us.list-manage.com/15P2H84dPVN?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0), a three-day immersive tour kicking off August 7th!
This one's personal, it's historical, and it's exactly the kind of conversation we needed to have right now.
**Listen or watch now:****🎧**[**RSS/Apple**](https://us.list-manage.com/JF4zQIpvwnp?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)**|**[**Spotify**](https://us.list-manage.com/vJxQ4lOb0KH?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)**📺**[**YouTube**](https://us.list-manage.com/hSHyOTpQOCr?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)
Want to be part of the Roots 50th celebration? Head to [roots50.org](https://us.list-manage.com/17jatw1LDhg?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0) for the full schedule and registration.
Thank you for being here,
Gloria

This year, on the anniversary of that book, a Tennessee school district from library shelves — in the same city that has a 13-foot statue of Haley holding that very book. This week I sat down with Chris Haley (Alex Haley's great-nephew) and Bill Haley Jr. (his grandson, and a 9th-generation descendant of Kunta Kinte himself) to talk about all of it — the cultural impact Roots had in 1976, the recent ban and its reversal here in Knox County, and what it means that we're fighting some of these same battles again today. Folks,
My name is Melissa Chaudhry, candidate for Congress in Washington's 9th District. I've pledged to support The 80% Bill -- 21 pieces of legislation that over 80% of Americans already support, across party lines. The good folks over at [https://The80PercentBill.com](https://substack.com/redirect/7f64e656-8bb2-48c0-8705-6a4c96218399?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) compiled this list for us.
Voters can also sign on, which is a statement of _not voting for anyone who 's not taken this pledge. _Highly recommend y'all join me!

Here's what's in it:

✅ Ban congressional stock trading
✅ End forever wars
✅ Lifetime lobbying ban for members of Congress
✅ Tax the ultra-wealthy & close loopholes
✅ Ban corporate PACs
✅ Audit the Pentagon (it's never passed one)
✅ Expand Medicare drug negotiation
✅ Fair elections & end gerrymandering
✅ Protect US farmland from foreign adversaries
✅ Ban corporate purchase of single-family homes
✅ Fund Social Security (lift the cap)
✅ Mandate police body cameras
✅ Ban dark money / overturn Citizens United
✅ 12 weeks paid family leave
✅ Release the Epstein files -- unredacted
✅ The DISCLOSE Act (follow the money)
✅ Close carried interest tax loopholes
✅ Right to repair -- ban parts pairing
✅ Ban junk fees & hidden pricing
✅ Congressional term limits
✅ Comprehensive data privacy (GDPR-style)

These aren't radical ideas. They're popular ones. The gridlock in DC exists because our representatives vote for their donors -- not us.

I'm running to change that.

Care. Courage. The Constitution.

body:
#

❗ Friends — To anybody who cares about ending gun violence in America, please don’t scroll away. This is an important July update from GIFFORDS. 👋
We’ll get right to it: With less than 100 days until the election, **[we need you to make your first online contribution to GIFFORDS PAC before midnight.](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q32026.gsDos-&refcode=em260728-1-b&t=1&akid=11672%2E3935704%2EvvjgCh)**

Here’s why:
Our gun safety movement is in peril with Donald Trump and extremist Republicans in office.
As we write this, Trump’s administration is trying to pressure the U.S. Postal Service to start freely delivering handguns — overturning a ban that’s been in place since 1927.
He also listed passing a nationwide concealed carry mandate as a top priority — which would mean people could carry loaded concealed firearms in public, in every state.

These are challenging times — but this isn’t the first time our gun safety movement has faced threats to our progress. We must raise hell to defend our work to end gun violence.
That’s why we need you to act today.

GIFFORDS is working tirelessly to organize voters and elect real gun safety champions ahead of the November elections, but we need more resources to share our message.
**Please make a contribution to GIFFORDS PAC today.** Polls are very close, and your donation could mean the difference between victory and defeat.

We get it. It’s a lot. And you might find yourself asking:**what is my grassroots donation actually worth?**

Derek, [**_when you chip in to Mark Warner’s campaign today, before our end-of-month fundraising deadline,_**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136157402/636537975/2134884402?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_EOM3QuickQuestion_260728_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4YjQxOTY5MC1hMThhLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=r_cWdYV0757Oh6fc0ov1I1wJa_pTNMDsz4VK0KM_wy0=) here’s exactly what it fuels:

| | Dear Friend,

In the spring of 1775, a handful of farmers and tradesmen stood their ground against the greatest military power on earth.

They didn't know how the story would end.

But they knew that freedom was worth fighting for.

The "shot heard 'round the world" set in motion a chain of events that led to the greatest experiment in self-government the world has ever known.

That's why I'm excited to share something special with you.

**The White House recently asked Hillsdale College to assist the Salute to America 250 Task Force in producing a new free video series, [_The Story of America_](http://links.newsletter.conservativedirect.com/s/c/gHO5slQJs4DWNykENWt3IOnDPCU26K2U1gM_neJLKh06FMFLSEFVYum4LnH78Af74Lb2z4gw2yZlS5ys-xaQyPdJzLiuWGyPk8IRQABoX5Y3QoERp0Btp25H8ml4bUqtTiD_CsVbDf0Z0Sh6wjUmvrRkHZ63fvX1UBQd1TxteBPa2JiztEVOuaQogfOjTELJFGyfPFmph09zDDUJKyvHBxNdaLM2uWk0VycVAUa03dAbEVUCSODQrCek4JD0mepP7tarH-yz7skBK5n8sIkSS-Vy7UdxnZ_WpWiS2Ph2274C9VF-7BQdVTy1DnEIGSiYpTWLnyuPvOOL7uZf_eRGdiy8y3BAh5bK6IrHCrsXHvnIW0vLs31gPIeRPxT_azMh9gQPlKpT0q9fxQKO6dZb3pYWz0DUKML2CsNvy1R3pqYF8y0JG3lgW2q-DcJQtg1NQVkjx3U1Gae9nG-adgCGqqjVIx6q5voZkq0sFRHi4p-L6silBGVL6N-mYUF6XCD2vGKlYAOI_qZf2cRDfBfBkifklgu7VuBzse42zlhSDVSHeOOa7CT9W5bLuh2_FNTjZTfnNs9SPkCC-pWEgcRMFTTRvCrPEgXgf9zy0ccf8hIZcbX3hZ-50oInZO8_JqKsbce-UG-zHh4l8X3dG18DN3IE6JG4yQt97LOcgVk-oBmsmBG12M525mCfse6iE7SUK0LOEGNTQs3Spr16kQ1wQkG4ncwE/Op-VS9Ps9bQq2sI2SFU_p6uPk1A0v_3b/23)** --a sweeping, episode-by-episode journey through our nation's founding in honor of its 250th anniversary.

As we approach the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence, this series invites you to learn about the principles, courage, sacrifice, and faith that made America possible--and _why this story still matters today_.

Filmed in the historic Indian Treaty Room in the Eisenhower Executive Office Building in Washington, D.C., each episode brings a pivotal chapter of the American story to life.

**Here 's a glimpse of what you can access on your journey at no cost:****
**

* **The Declaration of Independence** -- _Larry P. Arnn, President, Hillsdale College_
How the Declaration of Independence defines who we are--and what it still asks of us

* **The Formation of the Army** -- _Pete Hegseth, Secretary of War_
The moment citizen-patriots took up arms and answered liberty's call against overwhelming odds

* **The King 's Call to Arms** -- _U.S. Senator Mike Lee_
When imperial authority collided with colonial defiance--and compromise was no longer possible

* **The Culper Spy Ring** -- _Brian Kilmeade, Co-Author, George Washington 's Secret Six_
The remarkable story of ordinary Americans who risked everything to outsmart the British and save the Revolution

* **Story of the American Soldier** -- _Michael Knowles, Author and Podcaster_
A tribute to the forgotten men whose sacrifice secured American independence

* **The U.S. Marine Corps Birthday** -- _Vice President J.D. Vance_
The enduring legacy of courage, service, and sacrifice that defines the U.S. Marine Corps

Peter, Two lesbians walk into a conversation about defeating Donald Trump. **One is his niece. The other is a “scrappy little dyke” from Vermont who refuses to let bullies, billionaires, or wannabe authoritarians have the last word.** _Honestly, you HAVE to love it. 🤣_ Becca recently sat down with Mary Trump, Donald Trump’s niece, to talk about how we rally people during a moment this frightening, how we tell the truth about what is at stake, and how we still give people something to believe in. Mary said we need more leaders like Becca in Congress. Leaders willing to have difficult conversations, challenge old assumptions, and make it clear that Democrats are ready to deliver the foundational change this moment demands. **We agree. And with only three days left before our end-of-month deadline, we need your help making sure Becca can keep doing exactly that.** [_**Will you click here and chip in $5, $10, or whatever you can today to help us hit our end-of-month fundraising goal and deliver the good news to Becca?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136157558/636538511/687249954?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5NDkxZTU3MC1hMjhhLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Inj-_Epcg0I2KpYvhHDMbLXqz8ElXVwD_7M-_E7DRiM=) **[SEND SOME GOOD NEWS!](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136157559/636538512/687249954?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5NDkxZTU3MC1hMjhhLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Inj-_Epcg0I2KpYvhHDMbLXqz8ElXVwD_7M-_E7DRiM=)** Their conversation was funny and warm, but it was also deeply serious. Becca and Mary talked about the importance of meeting people with curiosity. Of trying to understand why someone voted the way they did instead of immediately deciding they are stupid, hateful, or even beyond hope. **A lot of people have spent years being lied to by politicians and media figures they trusted. Our job is to reach them with the truth, bring them into the conversation, and build an electorate big enough to win.** That is exactly the work Becca is doing in Congress. She calls out the bullies, names the threats we face, and never backs away from a hard conversation. | | | Dear Peter,
---
This good news has been a long time coming. We're thrilled to share that after more than a decade of partnership and restoration work, Save the Redwoods League has transferred the ‘O Rew Redwoods Gateway to the Yurok Tribe, returning 125 acres of ancestral land to its original stewards. The seeds of this milestone first took root in 2013, when Save the Redwoods purchased an old mill site on the degraded banks of Prairie Creek at the southern gateway to Redwood National and State Parks. It was a bold bet on what the land could become. Together with our partners, we imagined a future where the creek flowed freely again, wildlife thrived, visitors connected with the redwoods through an Indigenous perspective, and the land was returned to Yurok stewardship. Today,[ **that vision is a reality**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/136157862/636539474/1930876046?utm_medium=email&utm_source=ea-news-all&utm_campaign=project&sourceid=1170754&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9TVFJXTC9TVFJXTC8xLzg5NTc0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImIyN2ZlY2FiLWEzOGEtZjExMS1iMzM3LTAwMGQzYTE1NThjZSIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=J1Ne32QDNMFjLtoHQfP3QYvVj9dH1CyCag4pMBpQ2Nk=&emci=ddaa67fd-d486-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=b27fecab-a38a-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=1504551).
---
---
Many of our longtime supporters helped make that first acquisition possible. If you're among them, this moment is part of your legacy. And every supporter who has joined the effort since helped bring us to this day. Now, an exciting new chapter for ‘O Rew begins—one you'll soon be able to experience for yourself. On August 1, the gateway will open, welcoming visitors from around the world with Yurok-led interpretation, new trails to cherished redwood groves, and panoramic views of this revitalized landscape. clean_body: The bold vision for 'O Rew has become reality| | | | | | | | | | Dear Peter, This good news has been a long time coming. We're thrilled to share that after more than a decade of partnership and restoration work, Save the Redwoods League has transferred the ‘O Rew Redwoods Gateway to the Yurok Tribe, returning 125 acres of ancestral land to its original stewards. The seeds of this milestone first took root in 2013, when Save the Redwoods purchased an old mill site on the degraded banks of Prairie Creek at the southern gateway to Redwood National and State Parks. It was a bold bet on what the land could become. Together with our partners, we imagined a future where the creek flowed freely again, wildlife thrived, visitors connected with the redwoods through an Indigenous perspective, and the land was returned to Yurok stewardship. Today,. Many of our longtime supporters helped make that first acquisition possible. If you're among them, this moment is part of your legacy. And every supporter who has joined the effort since helped bring us to this day. Now, an exciting new chapter for ‘O Rew begins—one you'll soon be able to experience for yourself. On August 1, the gateway will open, welcoming visitors from around the world with Yurok-led interpretation, new trails to cherished redwood groves, and panoramic views of this revitalized landscape. Friend, let me tell you a bit about what this race means to me.
When I was growing up, I was a poor kid in a town full of poor kids. My family relied on food assistance at times. I distinctly remember when I was 13 years old, we didn’t have heat or running water, and I heard my mother quietly crying to herself, wishing she could do more for us.
After high school, I became a logger like my dad, and his dad, and his dad before him. When a greedy landowner tried to screw my fellow loggers and me out of fair wages, I fought back. A whole bunch of politicians, including then-first-term Senator Susan Collins, promised to listen, but they left us high and dry — and I realized that _nothing would change_ unless there were working-class voices in power.
So I ran for the Maine legislature, where I served 20 years, including six years as the President of the Maine Senate. It’s been the honor of my life to fight for working people.
I drove hours each way between the North Woods and the State Capitol, because that's what the job required. I won those elections in a district that went for Trump by 20 points, because up here, people care less about a label and more about whether you give a damn about their family.
Friend, I’m building this campaign the right way. With grassroots support from folks like you. I’m not running to impress the billionaires or the corporate class. I’m running for the mom who’s worried about how she’ll fill her gas tank this week. I’m running for the kid whose whole life will be determined by the quality of his education. I’m running to ensure every working family in Maine has the government they deserve.

clean_body: | | | Friend, Growing up in Allagash and spending years working 80-hour weeks in the woods to make ends meet, I know firsthand what working Mainers need from our government. And for 30 years, Susan Collins has failed us. Time and again, she has sold us out to Donald Trump and his MAGA agenda while pretending we’re too dumb to notice. And I’m sick of it. My name is Troy Jackson. I’m a proud Mainer, father, and fifth-generation logger. | Friend, let me tell you a bit about what this race means to me. When I was growing up, I was a poor kid in a town full of poor kids. My family relied on food assistance at times. I distinctly remember when I was 13 years old, we didn’t have heat or running water, and I heard my mother quietly crying to herself, wishing she could do more for us. After high school, I became a logger like my dad, and his dad, and his dad before him. When a greedy landowner tried to screw my fellow loggers and me out of fair wages, I fought back. A whole bunch of politicians, including then-first-term Senator Susan Collins, promised to listen, but they left us high and dry — and I realized that nothing would change unless there were working-class voices in power. So I ran for the Maine legislature, where I served 20 years, including six years as the President of the Maine Senate. It’s been the honor of my life to fight for working people. I drove hours each way between the North Woods and the State Capitol, because that's what the job required. I won those elections in a district that went for Trump by 20 points, because up here, people care less about a label and more about whether you give a damn about their family. Friend, I’m building this campaign the right way. With grassroots support from folks like you. I’m not running to impress the billionaires or the corporate class. I’m running for the mom who’s worried about how she’ll fill her gas tank this week. I’m running for the kid whose whole life will be determined by the quality of his education. I’m running to ensure every working family in Maine has the government they deserve. ** If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately. In solidarity with you always, Troy Jackson elects Democrats with disabilities. We fight to protect accessible voting, expand health care and Social Security, and equality for all.
